Monday: Did operator training for 1st and 2nd shifts. Main issue that Kraft is having is passing there accuracy test. The test consists of running a fixed UHMW cup that has been made to copy the real weight and size of product 10 times and checking that weight by subtracting the lowest weight from the high weight and it has to be +/- 3g. i.e. 148.6g highest and 143.6 lowest would be 5g difference and would fail the test. Also the average weight must be within .4g of the actual weight. i.e. 140g actual weight of product and after 10 runs the weight shows as 139.6g that would pass. Looking at the V-shaped bracket that supports the weigh table it looks way too close to touching the weigh drive unit and the other side has a larger gap. Waiting for production to end to adjust. Trained 2nd shift Maintenance. Received the quote for the line and it shows that for 5/6 oz cups that it was done at 150cpm (cups per minute) and the speeds that have to be done to create a gap for the product was around 200+ cpm. The rollers on the weigh table could have a bad bearing as when running it has more vibration than the infeed table. Took the belt off (white) and ran it and found it has no vibration. Visualized the sequence of how the relay board is reacting during production. When scale finds a combination the DCS2 outputs and then DCS1 outputs (Stroke on Demand). Packer outputs ILKSIG1. Error reject software: Installed software and started it in drain. Scale drains but there is no error signal output. When in production the error signal output when an overscale occurs is on 90,91 (Error Signal 2) moved the wiring over from 82,83 (Error Signal 1) to 90,91 and the chute moved into the reject position. When a proper weight was ready to dump the scale sat idle. Looked at the relay board and saw that the led for 78,79 (Discharge Completion Signal 2) was on. Moved the wiring from 78,79 to 28,29 (Discharge Completion Signal 1) Ran some product and watch it dump properly from the swing chute. I placed a span weight on a WH to give it an overscale and the reject chute went into the reject position. I removed the span weight and had a proper weight ready and it went back into the proper position to dump it into the HTH on the Distribution System.

If they want to use the current software and they need to drain, they need to press the drain button on the distribution system which opens the TH up top and moves the error reject chute into the error side and stays in that position until production begins and a proper weight signal (78,79) tells it to move back into the proper position.

The old software has them use 28,29 for the discharge completion signal and error reject signal 1 82,83 (which doesn't seem to do anything) So if they need to install the old backup of the previous software they will need to move discharge signal 2 (78,79 the new software needs to be in this output) to discharge signal 1 (28,29 the old software needs to be in this output)

To install the new software make sure that you open the folder that contains the software. it should contain these files and folders: BMDMU, BMFILE, BootCMD.bin, CwBootCMD.bin, CWCAL, ishida, MCU, RCU, rculib, rculoader.bat, SCDMU, tool, WcBootCMD.bin. Format the CF card to FAT32 and then place those files on the root directory (E:\ of whatever the drive name is on the CF card) of the CF Card. power off scale and insert CF card. Power on scale. Wait until the screen pops up with some buttons that say RCU and CWCAL and several others. Press the CWCAL button and then on the left hand side there is a drop down menu that says install new data or backup data. Make sure you backup data first. To do this press the back up data from the drop down menu and then hit the receive button in the middle of the screen. It will ask are you wanting to backup data to the CF card? Hit yes. After about 5-10 minutes the backup should be complete. Then proceed with installing the new software by pressing the drop down menu on the left side and select install new software and then hit the send button. This can take up to 10 minutes for it to complete. Once complete it will tell you that it is and just hit the ok button and turn on the scale. Remove the CF Card and then after 10 seconds power back on and the new software should be finished.

To install the backup software, insert the CF Card that contains the backup software and cycle power. Once you turn the scale back on it will bring you to the RCU and CWCAL screen which shows those buttons on the screen. Press CWCAL and then on the left side drop down menu the option for the backup will be on the bottom. Select it and then on the center of the screen it will show a send button. This will install the backup software. Once complete hit ok and then cycle power and remove the CF Card to prevent it from going into the install software screen again (RCU and CWCAL) and you should have the old software again.

What we have with the new software is the ability to reject errors to the error side to prevent them from being dumped into the trays. When a proper weight is dumped it will do so properly. When an error occurs it will reject it. With the new software the discharge signal on 28,29 needs to be moved to 78,79. The error signal needs to be moved from 82,83 to 90,91.

Detecting magnetic material will change the magnetic field causing the voltage to change. if Rx1 = 8 and Rx2= 6 then the sum is 2v.
If conductive material passes through it can create a secondary current, which in turn creates a secondary field.
Most food products are conductive, none are magnetic. If you run product longways into the head it will be much better for detection purposes.
Why is SS bigger than Fe to pick up? Because:
Fe is magnetic and conductive (+2 M and +1 C)
NFe isnt magnetic and is conductive (0M and +2C)
SS (316) isnt magnetic but is conductive (0M and +1C)
THS means Ceia food metal detector
THS/21 Single frequency (900 kHz); very high sensitivity, suitable with dry and neutral  products only.
THS/MS21: Multi-Spectrum technology; very high sensitivity, suitable with all products.
THS/21E: Single frequency (300 or 150 kHz); high sensitivity.
All models also available in slim line version.
All models are IP69K. Don't worry about low end models not being able to be washed down.
If 3 bars of chocolate are inside the MD head and it alarms all three need to be rejected for safety purposes even if 2 of 3 are not contaminated.
Multiple sensors on the rejection bin. Photocell to detect the product and reject it. Reject confirmation sensor. Reject check incase the product didn't make it into the bin. Bin full sensor.
Ejection timing: When product gets rejected the detected product will reject along with the product before and after it.
Ejection end sync area + Package length + detector length + Package length +  Ejection start sync area.
Push rejectors maximum line speed of 50-60m/min.
Sync sensor is always placed at the entrance of the reject bin. NOT BEFORE ENTRY OF METAL DETECTOR!
Ejection check photocell at the end of the reject box in case of pusher or air blast system.
All faults have to be reset by the reset button.
FS: In case of air blast or retractable belt ejections.
S: In case of Pusher ejection systems.
If its a push ejector then its S.  Air blast or retractable then FS.
0-6000mm If EM=FS dist. between the center of the probe and ejector
If EM=S dist. between the sync pc and ejector.
Check the distance from the center to the center.
Ej.end sync area* (EE) 0-250mm; distance between products.
Keyb alarm reset (KAR) OFF Disabling of the alarm reset using E button and Reset button located in the conveyor control system.
Keyb fault reset (KFR) OFF Disabling of the alarm reset using E button and Reset button located in the conveyor control system.
* Available only with Ejection Mode FS.
Bin Full (LF) ON bin full activation
Bin Full delay (LFD) 10 delay of bin full
Eject conf (CE) ON enable confirmation of ejection
Eject. check (ECK) ON ejection check functionality.
Ej.Check accuracy (ECKA) 30mm accuracy of the ejjection check functionality
Encoder check (EA) ON Activation of the encoder check functionality
Minimum speed (BL) 2-250m/min Minimum product transit speed.
Maximum speed BM) 2-250m/min Maximum product transit speed.
Phcell-MD distance (PD) 0-2000mm Distance between the side of the probe and the sync PC
Check photo dist ECPD 0-6000mm Distance between the side of the probe and the ejection check PC

Ej. ON resp.time (ERT) 0.000-2.000s To sync correctly the ejector activation, the parameter must be set to the nominal activation time of the ejection system. Response delay of the solenoid when an activation signal is generated.
Ej. OFF resp.time (ERF) 0.000-2.000s To sync deactivation time.
K Encoder (KE) 0-1000ppr Encoder pulse per revolution.
Diameter* (DI) 10-250mm Diameter of the encoder wheel.
Given the maximum speed of the line (Vmax in m/min) the encoder must be set for the number of pulse per revolution as defined by this formula
Bin Full input (IL) NC/NO  use NC
Air Supply needs to be between 90-145psi for rejectors
Only signals that are needed from Ceia to outside equipment is the Encoder sync signal Conveyor running signal.

Trained 1st shift employees on all screens and maintenance for the scale. Backed up all presets and machine settings.
Created a purge in the J-Box to allow moisture to be forced out of it. Greased all cylinders in Distribution System.
Changed pillars and spring in 11oz tool. Ran 145g of spring mix
Customer stated zero errors were occurring due to the fan blowing air in the direction of the DACS. Since the fan has been off there has been no zero error issues. Validated all Ceia metal detectors.
Spanned all DACS and did some training and PM's.
Customer stated zero errors were occurring due to the fan blowing air in the direction of the DACS. Since the fan has been off there has been no zero error issues. Validated all Ceia metal detectors.
Spanned all DACS and did some training and PM's.
Assisted with I/O wiring and installed drain plugs.

Tested interlocks and discharge signals between Bagger and scale. Cut bancallon strips for both scales. This will help prevent over scales. These strips will hang from where the existing ones are at and replace them. The apples will hit them and it will prevent it from going into the PH.  Customer said they will cut holes in the strips and mount them.

Ran +30 pallets in 8.75 hours. 40TPM overall average. 51 TPM with downtime and changeover  removed. Had a total of 9 changeovers. Ceia disconnect is broken. Lane A tamps were in the wrong position which was smashing trays. DFT #4 was bent causing bad weights  because it would hold part of the next charge.

Ran around 40 pallets today.  Had to install a flow restrictor on lane A swing chute because it was slamming hard against the stop. Operator zeroed DF with product on it which caused a clog on top of the DF pan and the nose of the infeed conveyor.

Had some startup issues. HTH #3 has a missing  spring in the holder. The blue  support brackets are loose at the end of the distribution system which has caused the chain to not be centered on the line for lane B. Lidding line had an issue this morning with the emergency stop which Dole will take care of.
Replaced a bad spring on HTH#3. It will now hold the drive arm on it properly. Replaced the plastic air blasts with stainless steel ones. Checked the line for anything loose broken or damaged.

Had no major issues for startup. Operator alerted me to the lane A reject cylinder on the swing chute was no longer connected to the eye bolt so it couldn't reject the error to the error discharge chute. Not sure how that could have came loose as I did an over view of the line yesterday. Replaced the eye bolt back on to the swing chute and verified that it worked.
RF 11 isn't vibrating well. Changed drive frequency to 46.2Hz. Works much better. Ran 36 pallets.
Startup had no issues. By the time I arrived they were averaging 5 pallets an hour. Ran +30 pallets today. No major issues.
Printed off data. Tested interfaces with Hayseen bagger.
Travelled to plant from home but had to turn around for a family emergency.

Heavy traffic in the morning (Parts of I-85S were shutdown due to wrecks which increased the travel time). Running a lot of products for a very short duration. A lot of changeovers which has slowed overall line speed per hour. Installed the new lamp for the Seal Vision System. Upon installation, a calibration is required if the display on the CamSensor screen indicates an obstruction which it did. Ran +30 pallets of several SKU's.

Ceia was having issues rejecting everything. Operator had it in the wrong program. 50/50 is the baseline program that works for all products. Label vision system was having issues with not finding the Search 1 target. The Dole bottom label doesn't have any graphics or symbols to use as a good reference so I used the barcode numbers since they are clear and large enough for it to pick it up. This is for the spinach with master pack. Denester A sensor for detected tray drop and blockage wasn't lined up properly and was causing it to not run. Adjusted the sensor to see the reflector. Must have been bumped into hard during sanitation or start up this morning. Denester B sensor for seeing tray blockage was off center slightly. E-stop was activated for 5 minutes and that took the line off line until we reset it. Had a clog in the HTH#3 due to the jam nut coming loose on the handle. It created a gap and allowed product to seep into the DFT and jammed. Found a loose jam nut on the eye bolt to the air cylinder. Adjusted the scrolls on the denester to help prevent the trays from hanging on discharge.

Running several SKU's (13 or so) Denesters are acting up again. Several trays are coming down crooked which is causing jam-ups. Tried to make adjustments but nothing seems to be working. Tried speeding up the actuators to drop the tray faster thinking that would help keep it from coming down as an angle. Denesters pulled offline and they are feeding trays by hand. Made some adjustments to the stack lift on the denesters. Will wait to put denesters back online when new scrolls arrive.

CCW had several over scale errors and found that the feed going into the CCW was way to much. Taught photo eye on the cross feeder to the proper depth and reduced the target weight on the DF. Seems that the values for the conveyors have been messed with and will try to put the proper values back in. Box machine and Labeller had a lot of issues today. Pallet count was the lowest its been in a long time. +20 pallets.

Spent most of the day trying to increase weigher efficiency by adjusting the feed. Photo eye on the cross feeder was working fine for spinach but going into 50/50 and spring mix seemed to change the depth of the product making it smaller. This was causing a lot of in and out of low product and missed cycles. Had to teach eye again and it seems to be a little better. Having difficulty teaching the eye the depth required to run better.

Had to adjust tension bar on the QX1100. The film was bowing causing it to ripple when it sealed. Changed DF target weight on the spinach to 325g due to the depth of product on the fastback pan. 92% C1 98%C2 for spinach. Had several over scales but managed to decrease them but lowering DFTW and adjusting nose on the fastback.
Traveled to the hotel. Family illness during the day so didn't go into the plant.

Worked with Tom Knodell and Carl Abols on the Fastback systems. Purpose of this trip is to observe product flow and attempt to come up with solutions to clumping and operator errors. Moved the PE on the metering conveyor from one side to the other. While it was on the other side it couldn't see the product coming off the hopper conveyor until the metering conveyor moved enough product to the incline conveyor and then the PE would meet and stop. Spent the whole day assessing product flow and attempting to change the vaules in the Allen Bradley inverters. We will make the changes early tomorrow morning before start up. Fabricated some bars that will be placed across the hopper conveyor that could be placed were the drum fills that hopper. This can cause any clumps from falling as a clump, instead breaking it as the product hits the bars. Will attempt to install it when the operators filling the hopper stop over feeding it. The amount of product being placed on them is causing it to overfeed the metering conveyor and so on. Fixing it at the begining will create a more uniform product depth which will reduce clump sizes and maintain good continuity.

Changed the parameters on the AB70 inverters to help run the fastbacks more efficiently. RF11 on the scale is again not working. Will order a new bracket for the plate support as it seems that the bolt doesn't grab the threads. Will attempt to replace that part after production or during a down day. Bent the bracket for the PE on the metering conveyor to try to measure it as the product fills in the center of the conveyor. Set PE on metering conveyor (Controls Hopper) to an acceptible product depth. Also found the photo eye is not controlling metering conveyor fully. It still stops it when depth is proper but the incline belt controls it more. Here is the logic in this order: The incline belt starts and if the PE on the incline that controls the metering conveyor isn't made, then the metering conveyor starts. The incline belt stops, the metering conveyor stops regardless if the PE is made or not. This will cause a gap on the line and needs to be changed in the PLC. Observed product flow during spinach run. Found that the product depth was good and that the duty cycle of the fastbacks are much higher. Two hours of production the CCW recorded only 10 overscales. Which is a dramatic improvement. I recieved a copy of the parameter change list for the Allen Bradley 70 inverters from Tom Knodell. I recieved word that Baby Romaine was running very good. They averaged 6 pallets an hour after we had left. 30+ pallets completed. They ran Spring Mix then 50/50 then Spinach during the time that I was here.

Came into the plant this morning with word that the CCW shut down during the night. Scott Rice (Packaging Superintendant) said that one side of the scale wasn't working and that maintenance spent several hours troubleshooting it. Once sanitation finished up around 8:30 I checked the tray sensors and verified that they work by looking at the I/O board #2 inputs for each sensor. Put span weights on the WH's and ran both sides with no issues. Since the line was down I asked the Production Supervisor if I could replace the RF11 on the CCW. I replaced the RF and verified it worked and also tested running actual product (Spinach). Ran 16 or so trays and confirmed that the system works. Since it was about 11:30 they decided to not run the line for the time being. I told them that it's ready when they want to run it. Some observations and fixes I made: I found some loose bolts on the Leaf Shroud tamp which is causing it to wiggle as it goes up and down. Also found that the Fastbacks are not secured properly to the floor. The most glaring one is the Metering Conveyor. Seems that the poxy they used or lack thereof didn't secure it at all. I could physically move the conveyor with a good amount of force and felt like I could tip it. Replaced the scrolls on the denesters but it seems that more adjustments are necessary since it still doesn't denest fully. Will work on adjusting tomorrow. Did further tests of the line and found no issues. Removed denesters to work on them in the shop.

So far this morning startup with Kroger spinach at 8:07 till 9:20 7 pallets. The only issues this morning are some product depth concerns. Scale kept going into low product. Adjusted DF TW but still have some inconsistencies. Turned infeed control off and it catches up with itself with random under (missed) cycles. Efficiency is around 93% for both sides. Over scales are almost nonexistent. We have about 15 people on the line this morning as well. Stoppages have mainly been on with waiting for boxes. Also the seal vision camera is acting up. It keeps displaying an obstruction error on the RCU. It's clean and nothing is in the way. After spinach was completed the line began to become sluggish. Constant clogging in the dipping funnels and HTH's. Lane B reject swing chute doesn't have enough air pressure or the cylinder is restricting the movement to move it over to the reject chute. Greased the cylinder and physically moved it back and forth and that seemed to help but it still seems that the air pressure is not enough. After production was finished for the day I found a loose bolt on the cylinder holding it to the swing chute. +30 pallets completed for the day.

Startup this morning was delayed slightly due to sanitation. Reject swing chutes are not operating at all. When they are supposed to I hear air escaping from the system. Some of the air blades that help move rejected product down to the buckets below are missing. I pinched the lines and found that the reject swing chute operate properly. Ran 12 pallets of spinach in 2.5 hours. Unable to get the print offs as they changed presets to changeover. Production ran rather well. Averaging around 4 pallets an hour with a reduced crew. Will return next week with Peiter Crape and attempt to get the Denesters on line.

Snow and ice on the roads impacted travel time. Seal vision system (SVS) was displaying an obstruction error on the screen. Calibrated the lamp and this fixed the issue. Unsure as to why this happens. Taught Weigher Feeder photo eye to keep bed depth a little higher so it will run consistently without starving the scale. Later during the day the SVS again faulted out. Will contact IE about the issue. Line was down for 45 minutes to fix a labeler fault. +25 pallets ran. After production finished I PM'd the line. Found some Loose Bolts on hopper fastback.

Worked on both denesters. Made adjustments tray support and scrolls. Installed on the line and found that the trays were dropping improperly. Also found the tamps were not working at all. Looked in the QX settings and saw that the PEC for filler 3 was ticked on. Unticked and the tamps worked again. Changed the drop delay for the Denesters from 520ms to 100ms. The reason behind the drop delay change is the size of the scrolls are larger. It takes less time to seperate the trays because the gauge is bigger.

Started production around 800. New person was loading trays onto the denesters which we had to train her. Had to position the sensor and reflector for Lane B denester since the trays falling didn't break the sensor which caused the denester to require a reset. Tightened guides for the trays to fall smoothly and reduce bounce. The bolts securing the DFT for Lane A position 1 snapped off. Had to remove broken bolt with an easy out and replaced the bolts. At the request of the Lead PMO he wanted the Denesters turned off. The normal crew that usually works this line isn't here today and they only have one operator running the entire line with a mix match of laborers. Trays going into the denester were nested together and too large of a stack. Explained again how to look for nested trays but it didn't seem to register. Denesters disabled for the time being. QX was waiting on Filler 2B but the scale had product and was ready for production. Found that the tamp on Lane B leaf shroud was stuck on the tamp resulting in the tamp not returning to home position for the prox sensor. Popped it loose and then tightened the loose bolt and continued production. Production has not been smooth today at all. A mixture of both equipment and personnel. Attempted to put the denesters back online with no better outcome. Tomorrow we will remove the denesters and see what adjustments can be made to better it. Removed the plexiglass from the old lamp for the SVS and replaced the new one. The newest one has some type of corrosion on the top layer of the plexiglass. After replacing it we did another calibration and the output displayed on the calibration screen (Green line) is solid instead of broken up.

IPS has a broken spring for the R1 robot. Also saw that 3 other springs are missing. Ordering more for tomorrow. Denesters taken into the workshop for adjustments to be made. Put the denesters back online and still have the same issues as before. Trays hanging up and too much bounce causing the trays to be in the wrong pitch. Operator changed several of the time and amplitude settings which has resulted in massive overscales (+700g). Put back to default and the line is running a lot better at that portion. case taper machine is having a lot of problems today. The operators have been at that side of the line trying to work with it and they have been neglecting upstream equipment. Seal Vision system has been working flawlessly today. Trying to tell the laborers to try not to push trays back toward upstream to put a lid on them as this results in the infeed sensor on the seal vision system to become blocked to long faulting it out. Seeing a lot of cases with less than 6 trays in it. Lids are not being secured properly.

Startup this morning went pretty well. Veteran crew mixed with some new people are laboring today. Ran spinach fairly well. Had some issues with overscales due to 50/50 mix was placed on metering conveyor with overloaded the incline and the weigher feeder.

Came into the plant this morning and the tool was being serviced in the shop late last night and someone dropped it from the tool rack. The damage is mostly cosmetic but the bone plate is bent, The shafts for the bone plate are bent. Replaced those bent pieces with the exception of the bone plate from the 11oz tool. Will compile a list of replacement parts for them to order. Installed the tool and the bone sensor #2 is outputting a product caught in tool error. Pulled the wire for 12 -2 on IF board #2 and it seems to work fine and hasn't missed a beat.
Travel day. Parked in long term 1 N furthest from main road.

UHMW side pieces will flex open dumping product to floor. Tyson sees this as a safety issue as some pieces are quite large and frozen and can hit people. This also is causing some cross contamination issues. Small product easily slips through UHMW openings. They have welded the hinge points shut to try to prevent this from happening.
Checked fastbacks product flow direction by looking at the shaft on the top left timing sprocket. Still waiting for electricians to finish up so I can start the checklist process.

Didn't get the line until 1900. Powered up fastbacks and the CCW. 3 of the fastbacks were wired backwards for incoming power causing the motor rotation to be wrong. CCW wouldn't drain. All the WH and PH wouldn't operate but the RF and DF would. Replaced the HUB board and this fixed the issue. Incline belt operates for less than a second and then faults out with an over current error. Solenoids aren't firing. Air pressure is fine. Found that the equipment was setup to run 110VAC but was installed with 24VDC solenoids.

CCW-RZ was missing a lot of cycles. Put span weights on WH's and did a combination test with a 595g TW and was seeing a lot of missed cycles. Stable time is 800ms, stable weight is .15g, and stable count is 1. Changed the stable weight to .35g and it improved greatly, didn't miss a beat hitting the test combination key. While running production I can't get higher than 80% efficiency because it will randomly miss cycles. Changed compensation from 1g to 2g and this has greatly improved performance. After 200 dumps efficiency was at 98.8%.

Came in today and found that the line was running at 66% compared to 33% the day before. Did see that someone changed the DF amp and time to 35/30. Works better at 75/50. Still getting compensation missed cycles but they happen once every 30-35 cycles. Removed load cell cables and reseated them also replaced the ADC board and saw that the weights are a  little more stable but still have some fluctuation. In talks with Kraft about them fabricating a barrier for the scale to help with drafty air that maybe the factor in compensation missed cycles. Running production has gone well today. Once I made changes first thing this morning, the efficiencies have never been below 98.7%. Troubleshooting the drive units I found that WDU 8 needed a PH and WH adjustment because the drive arm had a large gap between the roller and the arm resulting in the hopper not opening fully. WDU 7 wouldn't open or close the pool and weigh hoppers. Swapped with WDU 6 and changed the addresses and it followed the WDU. WDU 6  (used to be WDU 7) will be sent in for repairs. Adjusted PH 4 drive arm to open the hopper fully. If any hopper errors continue it will more than likely be product related. I've seen several chunks of triscuits that didn't separate and some are 6x6 or 8x8 pieces. Putting a plexiglass barrier around WDU 9-12 would help as I've seen it not stable while running production and show up as unavailable.
Installed counter weights. Leveled all equipment. Memory initialized scales.
Arrived on site and all equipment was installed. Checked voltages on scales and fastbacks. Bumped motors and powered on equipment.

Tested gates on distribution fastbacks. DFB #3 was locking up on closing. Applied grease to the shaft and that helped. Checked motor rotation on all FB. Leveled all FB and checked for gaps to prevent rubbing and hitting. Found that the disconnects that were installed on the 90E's were incorrect. They are a 3 pole switch. The drawing require a 4 pole switch to know if the disconnect is on or off in the logic for when the company is only running 1 or 2 scales.
Test ran Poppers @70bpm on scales 2,3. Disconnects should arrive tomorrow morning.
Installed the AUX connector for the disconnect. Ran 30g of Poppers @80bpm. 98.7% efficiency on scale 2 and 99.3% on scale 3. Tested AUX connectors and it works. PSD's signed.
Klockner 20518941 out of 30901640 power module assembly shell. Minoreck never got changed to what there providing.
38NO white wire left cable slot in panel 6
29NO white wire right cable slot in panel 6

Old distribution system removed and ready for new one to be installed when it arrives. Sealed up holes in j-box, panel 6 and scale to prevent water damage during sanitation. Tried to install new RCU and DMU software but ended up having software issues. Will continue tomorrow.
Installed IJ RCU and DMU software on the CCW. Had some issues with installing it. Came down to being a bad DMU.
Installed distribution system on line 16. Placed in line. Will level and land wires tomorrow.
Leveled distribution system and replaced peg and chain back on line. Control Panel placed on line will run wires to the system tomorrow.
Wired and cleaned up J-Box and mounted RCU.
Installed contacts for remote start and ran wiring to J-Box. Installed serial cable from control panel to HMI. Had to solder cables off and on to fit it through cord grips.
Wired remote start cables. Re-ran safety circuit cables for the peg and chain e-stop. Tested distribution system. Wires for remote start are XT4-17 and 18. Need to update the schematics.

Installed cable glands in the control panel for the distribution system. Ran an earth ground from the distribution system to the control panel. Tested output and input signals for the CCW, QX1100, and DS.
Cleaned up wiring in the control panel. Test ran spring mix and lane B works properly but lane A isn't. Software issue.

Testing line for production. Having issues with tamp servo motor slowing down. Found that when the safety switch for the denesters is pressed it causes the issue. Further more whenever one side is paused it will cause the same issue.  When this problem occurred it somehow lost its position and caused the main bracket that holds both tamps to snap and also bend the tampers. Replaced tampers and had a part made out in town for arrival tomorrow morning. Did some training with the designer of the distribution system.
Preparing line for production.  Ran 4 pallets of spring mix. Still having issues with software.

Ran 10 pallets of spinach. Went to lunch and returned to the machine being damaged from employee trying to start the equipment them self. Bent the tamper shafts as straight as possible. Used the 11oz tamper shaft as a replacement. Broke the bracket that holds the shafts for the tampers. Replacements for those parts came in so it was replaced instantly. Put a software change in the PLC that prevents the distribution system from starting up without being homed. Software is needed for the DMU on the CCW that will output the error signal from the WH and not from the TH when an overscale isis needing to be rejected.
Ran 27 pallets with a reduced crew. Assisted with production. DS ran very well. Boxes and labeller were consistently the issue for stoppages.
Drilled holes into the chain and peg to secure the distribution system. Tested update software for the DS.
Monday 4/2/12 545-700-1900 ( I paid for dinner lunch paid for by Tony)

First thing this morning the RCU for the CCW had a communication error. Must have been a conflict on the network. Removed Ethernet cable from Dole's switch that was connected to the hub in the CCW. Changed IP addresses back to default. Ran 25+ pallets with downtime being contributed to the box maker and labeler.

Startup was around 845 due to sanitation and a lack of crew for setup. Vision system has been working very well today. Removed the Ethernet cables from all of the equipment that makes it back to Dole's switch since the contractors doing the upgrades said it was causing a 'storm' (they're wrong) running production well. Distribution system has been exceptional.

Had some issues with the tool clamp not properly clamping to the top of the tool when being installed in the QX. Loosened 4 Allen heads and adjusted the clamp to allow it it be inserted into the tool. Tightened up bolts after it was clamped. The 2 nuts with the blue discs on them were loose on lane B side. Greased up the piping from the clamp to the tool to help ease it into each other. Had some gripper arm in/out servo errors lubed up bull screw and that fixed it. Ran +35 pallets.

Ran production of spinach and about two hours in the DS faulted out. DS wouldn't home at all. Error codes on the HMI labeled PCU Error Code 40960 with the Axis 5 with an error code of 20495. Checked to see if the ball screw itself was seized. Removed motor and turned it manually and it moves with no problem.  Found that the tamping bracket which is connected to the ball screw was off center and straightened it up. The home sensor was not being made so it couldn't home if it couldn't see it. Lane B homes properly but Lane A still will not budge. Cycled power for 5 minutes and then it tried to home but failed. When I moved ball screw it might have thrown the position on the encoder off. This is because when it tried to home it slammed up into the frame of the ball screw housing. Had to set the origin and then change the offset from 26.8mm to 8.4mm and this fixed the problem. Tested production and it worked properly. Installed new. CCW software that should properly reject the improper weight or error product.

Production started off bad. Somehow the carriage was trying to return and it bent the tampers as they were inside the HTH. The fault happened first, it being a clutch fault on lane A. I tried to reset to home and it was doing it very slowly then the carriage tried to return to home causing the damage to the tamps. Replaced the tampers and continued production. Had an issue with the line not operating but all interlocks were good but the DS just stood idle. Emergency stopped and reset to home and it worked again. IJ software works. The product being rejected out the reject chutes is over scales or errors. Still get an empty tray when the reject chute is being operated. Had some more in/out gripper arm servo errors but lubed the ball screws and it works again.

Ran production until we encountered an error with the DS. ran 22 pallets by 1330. The original problem was that Carriage A hit the limit sensor and needed to be jogged forward so the sensor illuminate indicating that it wasn't being obstructed. (NC) Once that was adjusted it would begin the homing process but then it wouldn't ever finish to run into production. After several hours of troubleshooting it came down to being a possible pinched airline for the pneumatic tamp on Lane A. All I did was jiggle it slightly and then the input on the HMI was lit up. The 4 inputs that have to be on after the homing process is sorted are 1:07, 1:15, 2:07, 2:15. (Slot 1, :07 input, :15 input, Slot 2, :07 input, :15 input) Homed and started DS into production. Shortly after starting production I left the area and returned to come back to a bent tamper on Lane B. Operator needs to E-Stop if they have a clutch fault so when we home again the interlocks should be reset. Lane B Carriage keeps hitting the limit sensor. Had to redo the offset. It was at 50.3 now it is at 52.
Started running production around 830 but Dole shut down the line due to the FDA ordering the plant to sanitize.

Worked with Michael Wagstaff from Ishida with the software issues. Some tampers needed to be replaced. The bars were bent. Adjusted the carriage A offset from 42.6mm to 46. The tamps on lane A were being bent because the offset for the carriage wasn't great enough.

Ran production. Did several trial and error runs with software changes to the DS. Moved the home sensors down a bit to allow the carriages to move back quicker. Light defuser replaced on seal vision system. Replaced infeed belt as well.

Running production. Went home early due to illness. Haven't had any drive issues with the swing chute. Took the photoeye sensor that was on the incline to tell the metering conveyor to turn off out of the equation. Changed the metering conveyor start time delay to 1.5 seconds.

Running production. During the run the bolt that secures the air cylinder for the reject side on the swing chute on Lane B snapped. Replaced and tested positions. Found that the part was frail on design. Changed the bolt on Lane A as a precaution.  Tested WH errors. Trying to troubleshoot why they are happening when it's not product related.

Ran production and monitored the line. After production which was around 22 pallets, I did further WH error testing. Installed the latest IOC software to help with deactivated heads in the tool. Installed new CW-CAL software for the CCW to stop missing trays after an overscale. IOC software previously installed was Q50118f - 31. Newest IOC software is Q50118 - 34. New IJ software is P2706B.

Ran production and monitored the line. Low staffing and no black hat operators made the line run very inefficient. Found that the carriage on Lane A kept causing crashes because it's up and down motion wasn't smooth causing the tamp to cause a clutch fault. Sprayed some lubricating oil on the shafts on the cylinders for both lanes. Installed infeed guard on the chain and peg. Put loctite on the dipping funnel doors for the carriage. Raised the carriages about 10mm to help prevent the dipping funnel from touching the trays.
Tamper bars arrived. Tapered holes for the detents (spring ball plunger bolt) for the clutch. Filed UHMW  edges so it would smoothly go up and down the shaft.  Monitored production.

Production started with no issues. Ran around 94 tpm for sustained periods of time. Ran 27 pallets in 7.75 hours (3.4 pallets per hour). Was on standby to run more production but instead the line was shut down due to not needing to run.

DS crashed around 2230 on 4/7/12. Found that the problem on carriage B was the home sensor was loose and not seeing the bracket at times so it would lose it position. The tamper bracket connected to the ball screw was replaced which in turn through off the sensors. Had to bring the sensors closer to the bracket for it to be seen. Tamp A traveled to far into the carriage which caused an over limit on the ball screw. The limit sensor at the top of the bracket was set to tight. Backed the sensor off the bracket and this helped after changing the offset to the tamp which prevented the servo limit sensor to activate (internal sensor) As a precaution all sensors will be removed and blown out with an air blast and then reseated to prevent sensor issues. Production started at 1100. Ran very well. By 1600 they ran 20 pallets. Having a PT100 error on the QX. Impression 2A is showing around 220 degrees Celsius. Looks like a connection issues that will go away when the tool is removed and installed again. Will spray some contact cleaner on the connectors as a precaution. First shift ended at 1700. Ran 23 pallets. From 1600-1700 the label vision system was having an issue with one of the presets. Changed the search image to something more defined than normal text. (chose the product code) This helped a lot but took 20 minutes off of production time.

This morning startup was delayed until 900. The servo for axis 5 (Tamp A) hit the limit sensor and just needed to be manually moved forward on the HMI. After that it homed properly. Product today has been not ideal. The spinach isn't baby size. Dole classifies this a teen spinach. Larger size has been more prone to over scales and missed cycles. Came back from lunch and the DS had another clutch fault. The tamper arm was way high and when it was reset to home it caused a servo error which required a power down for it to return to normal. The DS has been running very well since the making the sensor adjustments. Only clutch faults are occurring. (if the tamper arm was moved down instead of the stop forcing it down on the way up the servo error should be minimal at most) Lack of operators on the line have hindered the production speed. Rework was an issue. Labels not being placed on the trays and trays missing lids caused a lot of rework which slowed the line down and had to come to a stop to catch up. Ran 24 pallets.

Tampers were loose which may have cause the limit sensor to be made. Manually moved (HMI) the tamp down and tightened. Ran fine until about 1030 when Carriage A was hitting the limit sensor (over run) Found that the home sensor was made but the home position would change physically. Moved the home sensor closer to the bracket and haven't had an issue since. The carriage would move slightly forward and then it would think it was in the home position when it never left the bracket. This caused the limit sensor to be made which caused the errors. Had to adjust the home sensor on Tamp A. I would jog the tamp and the sensor would turn on and then off and then on as it descended forward. Adjusted and set it. Works fine. It is a little too close for comfort and I would suggest getting better sensors with a larger range. Ran 27 pallets.

Lane A Tamp had a bad sensor on it. Replaced it and 5 mins later it went bad. Problem is that we had to set the sensor extremely close to the bar so it would detect home position. We were thinking that the bar that was in there was not easy for the prox sensor to detect. We replaced it with the locally fabricated bracket and found that all it needed was a bolt head to detect home position. Found a sensor that was NPN NO that would work until replacements come in tomorrow for Mark Murphy to replace if necessary. Production began around 1100. Home offset was changed from 32mm to 8mm until the new sensor arrives then it will change back to 32mm. For some reason the sensor acts differently around the home position but it still works and has worked flawless since then.

Came into the plant with them having sensor issues. By the time I got down to the floor they had it sorted. Unsure of what the problem was since the denester on lane B was acting up. It would denest the tray cleanly and then the next tray it wouldn't. Took the denesters offline and removed the scrolls and then oiled the shafts and the cylinders. Put back on line with no change. Monitored production and saw on the QX RCU after a downstream interrupt that the TPM was 96.4. Took the denesters into the shop and removed the top cover. Moved the plate which holds the scrolls towards the frame making the space larger for the trays to not get bound up on the scrolls. Used a pneumatic toggle switch for the denester to test how it denests the trays. It looked good with no bound trays on the scrolls. Put back on the line and tried again. It worked a little better but still needs some adjustment. It still binds up and crashes.

Arrived on site to see that the DS was being looked at by the maintenance team. They said that the swing chute on lane A wasn't working. I looked at the servo error log and saw that all servos were errored out. Also noticed that the overrun sensor was made. Had to power the machine down for 10 minutes and then powered back up. Once the machine was back up I was able to move the swing chute from the overrun sensor. Reset to home and the DS was waiting on the QX Lane A. I couldn't get the line running so I cycled power on the DS, CCW, and QX. No change. I went through settings and saw that the Infeed Type was set to Continuous instead of Double Index. Once that setting was adjusted production started. After several cycles I started seeing under weights. I zero adjusted and started up again. Still had under weights. I looked at the swing chutes and saw that on Lane A that the swing chute wasn't lined up over the HTH. I looked at the drive arm and saw that the nut was loose. I went ahead and adjusted the eye bolt to bring the hopper closer to the HTH because the bracket for the sensors was coming very close to the overrun sensor. Ran production again and worked great. Scott Rice was adjusting a physical part that was unnecessary for him to change. The tool had an over heating issue with one of the impressions. I removed the tool and fit it and it changed from 3a to 2a. I physically pushed the tool with my hands to shake up the top and it connected to the impression. I was able to get all the heads working. One thing I noticed was when an impression is disabled the chances of getting tray length faults increases because the chain has to move as a double index when only one side can fit three trays it can get bunched up easily. Denesters are still offline until adjustments can be made. Tried running the denesters at different air pressures in the shop but I couldn't recreate the problem. The IP address on the label vision system was set incorrectly. I was using the RCU instead of the IOC IP. Changed IP addresses on the CCW. When I plugged in the cable going to Doles switch the scale froze and couldn't operate. When I removed it, it worked fine.

Came into the plant this morning with servo chain errors on Lane B. Loosened the tension on the chain and it works properly. The issues this morning caused the laborers to move to Line 18 and will resume production on changeover. Pulled the Carso Denesters from outside boneyard and removed the cylinders to replace the ones on Lane B Denester. Will install once I have a maintenance person with me. Had a mechanic with me while disassembling the denester. Suction cup on IPS has a crack in it. Replaced it and also had to adjust air pressure as the trays were being flung around. After further investigation the scrolls looked tight on one side and fine on the other. I adjusted accordingly but the tip of the scroll was very close to touching the edge of the tray no matter which direction I did it. I filed one edge of the scroll slightly to allow room for the tray to fall completely on the bottom edge without hitting the tip. I adjusted the guide bars to make sure that the tray would fall evenly. I placed the denesters on the line and ran mock production. I forgot to secure the HTH cylinder and the bracket it was connected to so that got bent from the carriage moving forward. It also broke two air fittings. I managed to straighten the bracket and replace the air fittings. I tested the denesters on Lane A and B at the same time and saw no issue with the denesting process.

Arrived at the plant with word that the line was down. Servo Chain errors on Lane B. Tension didn't seem to fix anything so I put grease into the shaft bearings via the nipples. Still didn't work so I changed the torque settings from +90, -90 to +110, -110 and this fixed the problem. I was able to physically stop the chain from moving by grabbing so it is safe incase something gets caught in it. Also saw that the tool bone plate wasn't dropping all the way like it should. I took the tool into the maintenance shop and found that the best thing I could do is remove the shafts at the corners which are used to detect if the bone plate is up before it gets to the proper position for the tool to be fully up to seal the tray and cut the film. Since the bone plate was never replaced from when they dropped it (and we had the sensors turned off because of this) I found this to be the only way to get production going. The denester on Lane B was again, acting up. I can't seem to mimic the problem in the maintenance shop. The line is ready to run production. I received instructions on installing the updated PLC program and will do this later in the day. Attempted to backup and install new PLC software but I couldn't retrieve a backup. Will continue tomorrow.

Had issues with the tampers on both lanes. Lane A home sensor was flickering which can cause it to not operate correctly (Clutch faults). Brought the sensor closer to the bracket which fixed it. Lane B had busted air fittings and a tear in the airline. Replaced them and it operates smoothly. Did find that the nut on the bottom of the bracket connected to the ball screw was loose on Lane B. Tightened and the DS is running well. Lane A tray sensor on the QX was a little loose which is more than likely causing the short length errors. Chad told me this morning that the servo chain on Lane B was acting up again but said that the torque settings reset back to +90, -90. He has it set to +115, -115. Conference call with Dole and Heat and Control about plans going forward. Line ran fairly well with some minor issues.

Came into the plant with some power faults on the chain and peg but I cycled power and that fault went away. Noticed that the crew that assembled the DS put the 11oz hoppers on instead of the 5oz. Replaced those and started production. After a few minutes the QX began to have infeed e-stop errors popping up. After observing where it could be happening I saw that the metal door gate magnet had a noticable gap between it. I removed it and put 2 washers behind it to bring it closer to the reciever magnet. Changed the Pre Ilk time on the motion preset from 410ms to 350ms and that has stopped crushing the edges of the tray when it arrives at the pneumatic tamps. Worked on denester B and completely broke it down and rebuilt it. Guides and scrolls should be in good working order. Will put it back on the line Monday. According to the downtime sheets written by Chad Smith the most concern he was having was with personnel and tray jams at vision, QX, and IPS. Vision system jams are from the lidders pushing the trays upstream. The QX is probably from a tray that didn't make it off the belt going on to the converger during a downstream wait or bad film on tray connected to another tray. IPS had some rails installed and a lexan cover to prevent laborers from getting their fingers caught on the belt transistion from the white to blue belt before the IPS. Adjusted the rails to allow better flow. Had a small amount of crashes in the DS but it wasn't even close to the main issue. Complaints are also with the product feed. They overloaded the incline belt which then needed to be cleared off. The scale feed maybe have to do with not having the denesters online. If one tray placer doesn't keep up with the chain moving and the other one does a better job the product on top of the scale is going to be very lob-sided.

Line had no issues during startup. Ran from 745-945 and completed 9 pallets of spinach. Put the denesters back online but still having issues with denester B. Tried to get it going but decided to pull it off the line to keep production going. Did have a problem with the photoeyes on lane B denester. The top PE wouldn't see any trays so it would fire on the cylinder to support the trays hitting the trays. I tried swapping cables but it still did it. I swapped PE and the problem was fixed. From my eyes the main issues with downtime have been with the labeller and waiting on product. Been having some short tray length faults on the QX. Some of it is from leafs on the belt. Trying to figure out the rest of the issue with it. Had some film snaps as well. I saw that some of the knives weren't fully returned and the reason was some film was stuck on the knife and kept it from returning fully therefore causing a film snap. Removed the film and pushed the knife back to the return position. Finished production at 1545. Completed 22 pallets (2.75pph) 30tpm with all downtimes included. Remove downtimes and base solely on uptime is around 4.2pph with an average of 45.4tpm. (This could be higher. Might need to do a downtime sheet tomorrow)

Another good startup. Did have some issues with Servo 1 on the QX for the chain and peg. Cycled power and manually pulled the chain. Film snaps continue to happen occasionally which can be fixed if they would order the new parts for the tool. Down time issues attributed to low product, waiting for product blends, boxes, labeler faults, some minimal DS crashes, and QX tray length faults. I am trying to get Dole to remove the bottom incline photo eye from the system because it does nothing but cause problems. The sensor is used to make sure that too much product from the metering conveyor doesn't get onto the incline belt while the incline is moving. The PE stops the metering conveyor when it sees a pile of product. This only causes gaps to occur and at times when it is bumped into in the dry room it causes the metering conveyor to stop because the eye is fixated on the pile of product from the metering conveyor. I have seen no evidence of this causing the belt to get overloaded. Made some adjustments to the scale for better combinations. At 13:36 production has ran for 6.5 hours. 20.5 pallets have been completed which results in 34tpm. Take the downtimes out of the equation (roughly 90 minutes to be fair) that brings it to 44.3tpm. Finished production at 16:20. Ran 26 pallets. Made 18,366 trays. 1,518 trays were bad. Average line speed was 34tpm. 6 changeovers. Each changeover takes an average of 15 minutes. Waited for product for at least 45 minutes. Labeler down for maybe 30 minutes. 30 minutes for boxes. 30 min for QX. About 3.75 hours of downtime. 4.9pph if you remove all downtime. 53tpm average. If you don't remove changeovers then it's 3.9pph/41.6tpm. Removed tool to bring into  maintenance shop to replace springs.

Had another good startup. Labeler was having issues during the morning run. Monitored production from 10:00 to 11:00 and noticed that the downtimes were due to several issues. The film snaps are happening because the knife from impression 3a is sticking out meaning the springs were not changed last night. Each time a film snap happens it is easily 5-10 minutes to get the QX going again. Labeler isn't setup to run in zero downtime mode. Each time the labeler runs out of labels or a fault occurs it can take 5-10 minutes to get that going again. Box jams can take a 1-2 minutes to clear up. Waiting on product and when the changeovers are about to occur. (i.e. trying to get the last trays and right amount of product on the belt to get that exact amount of trays needed to finish that particular run can really slow the line down) This could easily take 10-15 minutes to get 8-20 cases!) This all occurred during the  the one hour observation. We could have producted 2.5 to 3 additional pallets. Production started around 7:30 this morning and I took down some stats at 11:00: Trays produced 8,096 (12.4 pallets) Run time 3.5 hours. Trays per hour: 2,313. Trays per minute: 38.6. Changeovers: 4. Estimated speed when running with no issues: 88tpm (This number isn't exact by any means this is just and average of 3 minutes of continuous running at a time) Returned from lunch with the same issues. CCW is limping along with 3 clogged hoppers. Later in the run they decided to pull the tool out of the QX to replace the springs (WHICH COULD HAVE BEEN AVOIDED IF THEY REPLACED THEM YESTERDAY) Today

24 pallets have been completed since 7:30 to 2:30 with 6 changeovers. 7 hours of run time equals 3.4pph at least 2,222tph, 37tpm. Being generous and saying that downtime was 2 hours, equals 4.8pph at least 3,110tph, 51.8tpm. With all changeovers plus downtime removed makes it 6pph, at least 3,888tph, 64.8tpm.

Arrived at 715 as they were beginning production. They had a busted air fitting on Lane B Carriage. They replaced and when we started up a clutch fault kept occurring on Lane B. Removed the tamper and found that it was bent. The way it was bent tells me that when one of the airlines was busted it could have caused the hopper doors from not opening fully. The way the bar looks it has a nasty gash above were we drilled a little concave area for the spring indents from hitting something. I replaced it and also found that more fittings were destroyed. Also found that the tamp on closest to the QX wasn't tightened.(the one furthest from QX was the bent one) Finally got production rolling at 8:20. Ran the line for a little over an hour and during that time there were many problems with the labler, case taper, boxes, and some film snaps. They shut the line down due to the excessive problems and ran on line 18. Had a conference call with H&C at 1100 and went to lunch. Upon return they started the line again. The outfeed conveyor on Lane B was going very slow and the gripper arms were hitting the trays as they would move it from the tool to the outfeed belt. Lane A runs at full speed. Removed the belt and reset it and the problem went away. Changed the film tension from 50% to 28% and had no film snaps until about 2 hours later which were caused by the blue tray support pillars. Shut the line down about 15:30 due to the tool having issues. Since the line was down we had a represenative from Omron come in an update the PLC software in the DS. We have a backup of the old software incase of any problems. Replaced the servo driver and tested it by return to home and doing a test run. No issues. Removed the bottom tool from the QX and lifted the blue tray support pillars and found that the little UHMW cylindrical stop was loose and had worn one side down causing it to be high on one side and low on the other. It was high on Lane B and low on Lane A and Lane A is where all the crashing occurred. Need to order a replacement but was able to fit it back in and have it level. Tested by running a tray across the infeed belt on to the tool and onto the outfeed belt and it was smooth.

Came in this morning and found more air fittings have been busted. Also found that an air cylinder was bent badly. According to one of the operators the hopper on Lane B fell off and was bent out of shape. This can attribute to the cylinder being bent as well. Took the 5oz carriage and hopper into the shop to work on it. Used parts from the 11oz carriage to replace the bad cylinder and air fittings. Put back on the line and did a test run. Everything looked fine until about 10 cycles in. One of the tampers wasn't secured properly (Scott Rice's fault) and it hit the other cylinder on the carriage and broke that. If the tampers aren't secure they can wobble a lot and it will cause problems like so. I know that the tamper hit the cylinder because can see UHMW shavings on the threads and also a crack in the tamper corner. Managed to get the line running fully about 1300.

Came in this morning with no issues with the line. About 930 Lane B had a servo chain error fault. Couldn't reset it. Here is what I did: I changed the torque settings from -115/+115 to -200/+200 (max) and the following error was at 50000. It still wouldn't move. I manually moved the chain and it was a little difficult but compared to Lane A it is a lot smoother. Tried running the QX on just Lane A but the setting didn't work Lane B still was trying to move and kept faulting out. Took the line down and tried swapping the comm cables and changed the address from servos 1 to 2 and 2 to 1. No difference so the driver is good. I unplugged the motor at the chain and peg for Lane B chain and reset it. Tried moving the chain back upstream to see if it is a mechanical problem. Tried moving the gripper arms in/out (suggested by Simon) and then moving both chains (A+B) with no luck. They have no spare motor for the chain but I found one that can be used without it being fried from the higher current the motor requires. (2.5A and no other motor except one that had a higher current rating (5.2A)) and connected the encoder and power cable to it to see if it would move and it does. The motor I tested will not fit in the gear box because of the size of it not fitting in the enclosure. I removed the presumably bad motor from the gear box and tested to see if it moved and it does. I noticed with the higher rated motor that the hall sequence error went away. With the original motor the sequence was never lower than 6 on the servo info tab in the QX. I still don't have a 100% answer as to what is causing the problems but I believe I should have them order a new motor as a start. I managed to get the line running with just Lane A. I turned the option on and also went into the misc section in the settings menu and selected single chain infeed and disabled all head and turned off all knives on the B side and it worked fine. At the moment they are running one side rather efficiently at 46 tpm. They have a stirrer up top on the mezzanine to keep product in C1 on the CCW.

Startup was good this morning. Ran 6 pallets of Sassy blend (arugula, spinach, reds) which is the hardest to run and ran 4 pallets of Tender Garden. Labeler was faulting constantly (Chad wasn't there at the time) which hindered the efficiency of the line. When it was running well it was constantly pumping 46tpm without issue. Once production was over I worked on the denester for lane B. I replaced all the cylinders and setup the guides. On monday I will ask Dole to order a motor for Lane B chain and peg.

Startup went well this morning. Averaging almost 3 pallets an hour with only Lane A running. Checked with Dole about seeing if their servo motor has come in. After contacting Hayward, Dole signed for it 5/17 but didn't finish the process of putting it in their inventory which would have fixed this problem a lot faster. After replacing the motor the chain and peg is now moving. Production is running on both Lanes. Tomorrow they will put the denesters back on and see if the problem with Lane B denester has been resolved. Had several film snap issues and saw that the film tension was set to 95%. Reduced to 50%. Had an issue with the tool losing communications with the thermocouples. Removed tool and fit again and the error was still present. Removed tool again and sprayed the connectors down. A lot of water was built up inside the female end of the connectors (connected to the body of the QX). Fit the tool and the errors went away. Also the hall sequence error went away with the new motor.

Had a good startup this morning. Did have some clutch faults on Lane B chain and peg. Adjusted the tension as it was a little loose. Installed the denesters and they both worked properly for about 30 minutes. The denester on Lane B is going back to not separating the tray properly. It will hang on one edge one time and the next time the other. Can't go more than 3 trays before it starts to fault out again. HTH 3A is bent pretty badly. It was bent before on Friday of last week but somehow it got bent again. More than likely a new HTH will need to be sent over. Labels are being put on improperly causing the label vision to go haywire rejecting everything. Operators were telling me that the QX was having several film snaps but I would monitor it and would never see them. 18 pallets today from 7:45 - 16:45. about 2 pallets an hour. Downtime due to boxes, clogged hoppers on the CCW, denester testing, clutch faults in the beginning of the day (resolved) labeler faults, label placement, and waiting on product.

Came into the plant today with word that Line 16 will not need to run today due to low product volume. I took parts off of a HTH from the old DS that had the 45 degree which matches up nicely with an 11oz hopper body. It's a nice angled shot into the carriage hopper. Also replaced the servo connectors with crimps for sanitary reasons. I replaced the bulb in the Lane A control panel but it still doesn't work. Wiring may be bad. Tool is being cleaned out. Went ahead and checked for broken springs and found 2. Removed the sensors from the bracket on the clutch as this will elimated safety clutch errors. Adjusted the denester guides as I did see that they tend to hit the trays. It was tight which could be the problem. Will test tomorrow.

Late startup they were having a lot of underweights and found that they had tried to put the bad 5oz HTH on. (Scott Rice) I replaced that with the modified HTH that I made from the old DS and had no issues. The bad 5oz HTH doesnt close the hopper gates all the way, therefore, leaking product onto the chain and peg. Someone had turned off the reject for bad labels on the LVS so a whole pallet of spinach didn't have bottom labels. Chad Smith isn't in today so the line will only be ran by one operator (Ziporia) and an inexperianced lead of some sorts (Jess). The belt on the outfeed of the SVS is loose and will have maintenance take care of it. Case taper and labeler are having issues but the labeler is the only one causing the down time. Was having spurts of low product but the photo eye at the incline was pointed right at the product on the metering conveyor so only little bits of product at a time were coming onto the incline belt. Completed one pallet in less than 9 minutes but during that time the case taper was acting up and the laborer stacking boxes was struggling to keep up. Right after the pallet completed the labeler faulted out again. 15 pallets ran today in 6 hours = 2.5pallets and hour. Some of the faults were gripper home fail which needed the ball screw to be broken loose and manually driven by the belt to clear the fault, tray length errors which is being a nuisance, some film snaps, drive belt on SVS outfeed being loose, infeed photo eye on the incline belt needed to be moved, infeed photo eye on the SVS wasn't aligned properly, and scale efficientcies along with the infeed control being off didn't help either. DF weight was set really low (250g, ~ 450g is best) Operational issues are boxes, waiting for product, labeler faults, case taper (not causing the line to go down but hurts pallets out the door) scale not effciently setup preset wise. The line will stop sometimes due to a problem and it takes 3-5 mins to get it back rolling again. Little operational faults really start to add up. After production I have adjusted the sensors for the tray sealer, removed a bracket covering up a driive belt for the infeed on the LVS that was giving off a really high pitch squeal, attempted to get the CCW connected on the network but still can't get passed the comm errors when I plug in the ethernet cable connected to the switch upstairs. Dole's main person that works with the ethernet cables and switches is out until Tuesday. Will try to work with Tommy Parker about troubleshooting the communication problem tomorrow.

Startup this morning was delayed due to a bad belt on the labeler outfeed. Took 30 minutes for them to replace it. In a 3 hour run of spinach they completed 11 pallets (3.6pph). With downtime removed (71 minutes) brings it down to 1.8 hour run time averaging 6.1 pph / 66tpm. Very solid run. Attached is the downtime sheet written by Chad and Adam. The photoeye handle for the labeler was broken after the spinach run. Maintenance will be responsible for fixing it. By 1330 they have completed 18 pallets. While on spring mix they've been running into a lot of problems. Chad Smith isn't on site during this run but should be back later in the day. A lot of the tray length faults have been from leaf on the line. I checked the guides in the DS and the tray tends to move around to much so I tightened them. Adjustment to the tray sensor has been adjusted and seems to work better. I monitered the trays going into the tray infeed in the QX and noticed that a lot of it is leaves getting on the belt. They don't have the normal manual tampers working today so I explained that they need to make sure that no leaves are on the chain. Waiting on product a lot during the spring mix run. Had an issue with the UHMW stop that is part of the blue pillar tray supports in the tool. We need to have them order some replacements to stop having to make adjustments to it. What happens is the UHMW has been worn causing it to be uneven which in turn causes one side of the blue tray support to be higher on one lane and lower on the other. This causes crashes because the trays rub against the yellow gasket material instead of sliding on the blue pillars. Managed to run 20 pallets.

Came into the plant with the tool being removed because of the electrical pins on it being bent somehow. Took some needlenose pliers and straightened them. Fit the tool and it now it works properly. Was having issues with the DS. After 3 or 4 cycles it would 'emergency stop' due to a timer being exceeded on the carriage. The error was on Lane A. I sprayed some lube on the carriage cylinders and the problem went away. Main downtime concerns are the usual; waiting boxes, box machine, labeler, waiting on product. Some film snaps but not causing a lot of downtime, minuscule at best.

Came into the plant this morning with gripper in/out servo faults. I tried to adjust the gripper arms on the ball screw not knowing that the home sensor was able to be adjusted. (Thought it was fixed) Once I was able to adjust the home sensor I properly aligned both gripper arms and made sure it wouldn't hit the tool in motion. Finally began production around 1400. On the start of production the DS began to freeze up while in production. It always seems to lockup when Carriage A ready to move forward after the HTH has opened and Lane B is on the return home but only makes it halfway there. Looking at the drive status tab in the HMI it gives the errors for Axis 5&6 of 53263 and for Axis 1 its a 204XX number (I'll try to catch it Tuesday)  I sprayed the shafts for the carriage cylinder and it still occurs. After 5 minutes of doing that it seems to have gone away. The next step would be to just lubricate all the shafts in the mornings to prevent it from happening unless there is an underlying issue. While production was going it was running pretty well. Returning Tuesday.

Startup was good. Still having issues with the DS abruptly stopping mid-production on startups. Will lubricate all cylinders to see if this will help. Camsensor on the SVS HMI is blank. Not sure what caused the problem but it is running in conveyor mode. Denesters are ready to be put online. Trying to install them for changeover. Production was running horrible due to operational issues. Labeler faults, waiting on boxes and product often.

Came into the plant with the Ceia not detecting product as the settings were low on purpose. I changed the settings to 280 sensitivity and 0 TX and the Band at Medium. It was alarming constantly. I changed the TX Channel from 1 to 2 and that took care of it. Ran test samples through the head and it picked up with no issues.

Came in this morning with the Ceia settings adjusted again. Put the settings back to the way it was and saw that it was alarming again. Found that the safety hinges that cover the air cylinder to drop metal detected product from the belt was touching metal somewhere in the closed position. Opened up fully and it works with no issue. The Ceia runs very smooth.
Came into the plant with no issues. Running product fine and picked up test sample of 2.0mm FE, 2.5mm NFE, 3.5mm SS.  Travel home.

Came into the plant this morning and production had just started up. Had a solid morning by running 16 pallets by 1200. Production has lost momentum after lunch with only 8 there after. Total of 24 pallets today. Ended production at 14:30 due to no product available to run. Made a change to the DF frequency. Set it to 39.0Hz/40.1Hz and it makes a major difference.

Had issues this morning with a bad sensor cable to the photo eye on top of the fastback. Because of that issue production didn't start until 9:00. Had to remove the tool because one of the impressions lost communication and caused it to over heat. Replaced tool and it worked fine. Line today is only being run by one PMO. Was going to put the denesters on line but they were no where to be found in the building. They were placed outside of the plant in the boneyard and was approved by the maintenance manager. Production finished today at 16:00. Did 20 pallets. Removed tool and had a maintenance person with us to take it apart and show him some of the innerworkings of it. Checked for any problems with impression 3b, didn't see any. It was deactivated because it was hanging the tray which caused some crashing.

No production today. Tested WH errors for both sides of the scale. We swapped the power going through the DC Fuse boards from PH/WH 1-8 to PH/WH 9-14 and the problem followed over to C1. We tried to swap DC Fuse board for BH 1-8 & TH,RS,DTH to PH/WH 9-14 to see if the WH errors would go away on C2 but it wouldn't. Loaded IJ software 2706B and IJ RCU software and it still has WH errors. Had some difficulty getting the software to load with the IP addresses back to normal. Ended up hitting the clear button on the RCU update screen to delete the RCU parameters to get it to work. Tested denesters and they work fine.

Production started around 800 with the DACS having a pulse error on the reject conveyor. Scott Rice said if line 16 is going to run then we better get out there and fix it for them. All it needed was the reject conveyor moved from hitting the infeed of the seal vision system. Ran with the denesters but after 1.5 hours it wasn't working efficiently we removed them from the line. Ran 27 pallets. 36.5TPM 3.4 PPH.

Gripper arm on Lane B is bent. Bent it back as much as possible and now it doesn't hit the tool when sealing occurs. Had to make adjustments to the photo eye on the DACS and SVS. By 12:00 the pallet count is 14. Had a broken belt on the case taper infeed. Waiting on product, boxes, and labeler faults as usual. Spring mix ran very well but was hindered by the usual suspects. 9 hours of production with 27 pallets ran. 32.4TPM 3PPH. Lane A wasn't counting trays as it came onto the infeed conveyor the trays were pushing other trays forward. Checked the photo eye. It properly goes off when a tray is in front and on with nothing obstructing the reflector. Checked the signal on the I/O page and saw that it would never turn off (signal). Replaced the photo eye and it would properly signal. Tested with some production and it works accordingly.

Good startup. Still just one PMO and a Lead. Waiting on boxes, product, labler faults as usual. No operator was on the line from 1450 - 1520 (was later told that Adam on line 17 was keeping an eye on it but wasn't going to be able to run two lines). Line ran quite well with me just watching over it. Did have a short tray fault on Lane A and a LVS jamup from a skewed tray at the outfeed (lid wasn't on properly) and that was about it. Ran 2 pallets in that time. This whole week had 2 problems which needed to be fixed for the line to run. A sensor cable for the Fastback and a new sensor for the tray sealer to count the trays. (maintenance issues) A lot of product issues today. Only ran 20 pallets as Dole wasn't able to keep up with the demand for product.

Bad startup this morning. The SVS had several servo faults. Found that the servo motor was coming loose from the housing. Tightened back up and adjusted the belt. Started production but then had a heater error on 3a removed tool and cleaned with a brillo pad. Fit tool and then it went to 3b. Disabled 3b. Found that the reject was turned off for the LVS. Distribution system was having a lot of clutch faults. Excessive product was getting into the HTH which in turn cause clutch faults. Saw that it was only happening on Lane B side (C2). Went up on the mezzanine and saw that WH9 wasn't properly put on which was having a lot of product leakage. Placed WH back on and had no more issues with clutch faults. The Thomson drive for Lane B carriage housing has a pieces of a bottom cover hanging off. Later on during production the bottom tool needed to be removed because it hasn't been cleaned out in a long time. Several cut pieces of film were at the bottom with a lot of product in it as well. WH11 was causing clutch faults in the DS because it was bumped or messed with because there was a lot of product coming down to the HTH. Ran 15 pallets which concluded the day.

Had to increases the following error slightly on the SVS as it did have a servo fault this morning. 20000 to 30000. Ran around 4 pallets before they were having issues with the DS. Having trouble with clearing a fault on the DS. I'm not certain how the issue was caused to begin with but Chad (Lead operator) told me that the DS had a tray crash and one of the laborers on the line frantically pushed several buttons on the system to stop it. Chad couldn't clear the error on the screen so he shut it down. Before I powered it back on (not sure how long it was off) I saw that the charge LED's were not lit so I assumed that any servo error on the system should be reset. On power up the reset button keeps flashing. All doors are shut all sensors are working properly all E-stops are not activated. The errors on the HMI are:
M16- Emergency Stop Relays NOT OK :10,03
In the Servo Axis Status Servo Errors are on all but Axis 4. All Axis have errors and all the Drives alarmed.
Servo Axis Status for all Axis are 20495

Came down to KF 22 needing to be jumped across on 13/14 (NO) By doing this I was able to start the system. I was thinking that the Relay was bad but as I came back down to the floor to troubleshoot, it powered on and worked properly. I was unable to recreate the fault even after several power cycles. I did remove wires from the pilz relay and reconnect them. Unsure of that fixed it.

Came into the plant and was told that startup would be delayed until Line 18 was finished. They never started the production and sent the operators home for 16. I did a quick checkup of the line for production tomorrow.

No production today. Tried to test WH errors but I can't do it alone. I had asked a maintenance person to assist but they got called away to fix a problem. I waited till after lunch and then find my help not here anymore. I tried to check the voltages on UO3, UO4, OU5 but it is very cumbersome. By the time I get up to the mezzanine to try to position myself to read the output voltage the C2 which is where the WH errors occur, faults out completely.
