I will try to do this on a later day when I can get some dedicated assistance. Tested DS in dry cycle and ran into some issues. Found that I needed to spray the sensors down at the carriage A side because it was having a hard time seeing the home sensor. Did also find that the problem I was having two days ago was a door switch that wasn't showing up on the HMI. It was showing up two days ago but for some reason the door switch on Lane B middle door is malfunctioning (transmitter side). Replaced the guard switch and tested it. It shows up properly on the HMI. Ran the DS in dry cycle for 10 minutes with no issues.

Came into the plant with the SVS having test conveyor issues and pins bent on the combitac connector for the tool. Tried to bend the pins back into shape and they snapped very easily. Didn't have enough spare pins to replace them. Took apart the 11oz tool and cut the pins that I needed and soldered and heat shrinked the cables. Fit the tool and it all heaters work. Haven't been able to fully troubleshoot the issues with the SVS as working on the tool has taken the whole day and was trying to get production rolling due to the huge orders this weekend. Had to adjust the gripper pick from 37mm to 32mm as it was crashing into the trays causing crashes. The LVS bottom light strip for the camera was bent out of shape. After finally finding the right position for the bottom label to be visable on the RCU we were able to run the line from end to end. At the moment they have 2 extra laborers on the line to assist with picking up the trays and placing them on a table and the other person putting them on the conveyor belt to bypass the SVS. Sanitation has been removing the belts on all the equipment according to Chad Smith and Scott Rice. I don't know 100% who is bending things out of shape whether it be setup in the morning by the operators or sanitation at night but it is really hurting the line. DS has been running great. I went back down to the line to check on it and found no operators. The line was running decent but there was no authority figure to delegate when things went wrong to be taken care of.

Checked power for 24VDC for servo drive and power for the motor on the SVS. It was only reading 2.2VAC and it should read around 300VAC. Checked power for the test head servo motor and it was 299.3VAC. I swapped the cables from the test head to the conveyor and it read 2.3VAC. Seems that the motor may have a break somewhere internally. When production finishes tomorrow I will swap the test head and conveyor and see if it changes anything. Ran 17 pallets and then the DS started acting up. It will start at the home position and the HTH will open and the carriage will advance about halfway through the HTH and then slow down for about 50-75mm and then speed up again and the tamps will come down properly and then return home. Then the carriage will return and at the same point it will slow down again for about the same distance and speed then the HTH opens and product doesn't make it into the carriage hoppers. Then it returns home then advances and repeats it again. I've shut power off to the DS and let it sit for 10 minutes. I have jogged it and seems to go back and forth smoothly. I have done a manual movement carriage advance it will mimic what it does in production with it slowing down on the advance. Same with the return. However, when I do an advance and return it to origin on the carriage jogging section it will go back smoothly but at the reduced speed that occurs when you hit the origin button. I've removed the encoder and power cables to the carriage servo motor and cycled power and powered off for 25 minutes. Nothings changed. I've tried swapping drives and that caused more of a problem. Swapped them back and just had C2 running on the CCW. So for them to run production they have one person up on the scale moving all the product to C2 and one person placing trays on Lane B, the people tamping are moving trays equally to run into both sides of the tray sealer, and two people maneuvering trays around the SVS. Tomorrow I plan on swapping the motor on the SVS and possibly replacing the Thomson drive on Lane A.

They were still running production by the time I came on site and didn't finish until 1400. Once production finished I removed the belt from the Thomson drive and rotated it by hand. I had 2 other people rotate it and they said they didn't feel much resistance as they turned it. Turned the DS on and reset to home which caused the servo motor to rotate continuously and I didn't see any jumping or binding in the motor rotation. Put it all back together and did some test runs and still have the same issues with it seizing up and binding in generalized areas. Saw that the collar wasn't fully on the shaft connected to the Thomson drive and placed it fully on it and locked the bolts down. By doing this it worked very well for about 3 minutes then began to act up again. Took a break from the DS to work on the SVS. I thought that the motor for the test head was the same as the conveyor motor but the test head is a 275 and the 175 is the conveyor. Replaced the Thomson drive and still had the errors. Checked input signals on the HMI and didn't see any flucuation (hard to tell if it was due to the speed it was running at in dry cycle) I did a test run and didn't see any issue with it. Also manually jogged the carriage and didn't see anything wrong with it. Will continue tomorrow.

Had a phone call with Michael Wagstaff and Simon Cuthbertson from IE and they were saying the only thing that can cause that problem besides the servo motor or driver is if the Dipping Chute signal turns off in motion. I was told to slow down the velocity in the settings for carriage A and by slowly do it lower and lower to see if I could spot when the carriage binds and see if the input goes out. I had a Dole maintenance man yell when the input went out. After a few cycles of running in a low velocity we were able to spot it. I swapped sensors from Lane A to Lane B to see if it was a sensor issue. The problem still exists on Lane A. Tried a new cable and found that the problem went away. Ran in dry cycle for 30 minutes with no issues. Removed the old cable and did find a break in it. It had broken through the insulation and was causing a small intermittent open in the wire. The break in the wire was inside the energy chain (Dyno track) so I don't think that over time it would do that much damage to the cable. It looks as if this was cut by something. Went to the SVS to try to get that running. Checked voltages on the drivers. Input voltage was 200VAC. There was no output to the motor like something in the drive was not telling it to move. Loaded last known good settings and at that time the SVS would properly fault out but still wouldn't move the belt. (It would run in production but no servo error would showup and the belt didn't move). Ordered new servo driver and motor for delievery tomorrow.

DS kept faulting out randomly. We check out all the sensors. I did see that the home sensor on Lane A Tamp was flickering but it shouldn't effect the system as the carriage should return normally. Adjusted the sensor to move it in a little bit closer. We saw that on the servo driver for carriage A was an error of 21 (encoder) We removed the enncoder and set it back in place. Since then we haven't had any random stoppages. Changed the motor on the SVS and saw that it was working. Tried mounting the motor and had some issues with the test head not going up all the way (It's disabled but we keep it up with zipties) Managed to keep the test head up. Made several belt tension adjustments for tracking the conveyor belt but kept getting servo conveyor alarms. Raised the torque from -50/+50 to -200/+200 and follwing error from 10000 to 50000 and still got errors. Did find on Lane B carriage dipping chute sensor cable has a break in the insulation at it's most bent point inside the energy chain.

Tried to get the SVS going.  Replaced the driver and loaded parameters but couldn't get the system running. Ordering parts (cables, drive, motor) for tomorrow to replace all at once. Tried running with the belt off, the motor on the gear head, and just the motor itself with no change.

Continued trying to get the SVS up and running. Contacted IE about it. Bus voltage is at 292V at its highest and 55V at its lowest. +300V is best +280V it can run. Anything below that it won't operate. Current is around .02A at its highest and .001 at its lowest. Managed to get the motor to operate but faults out every 10-15 minutes.

Came into the plant with the SVS still only working for 10-15 mins. The denesters on the line are running very well and have had only little problems which are corrected easily. Lane B in the DS is having a lot of clutch faults always occuring after an error reject. Found that WH12 had a WH error and an auto zero error. After correcting that it ran just fine. Still have PT100 faults. The problem is occuring in impression 4b. Found that the servo motor giving us the fault of 132 was occuring (likely) because the ethernet cable connected to the motor was being placed in a switch that was also communication data which can and more than likely cause comm errors which was resulting in the motor stopping. By 1330 they have completed 15 pallets of spinach. When disabling an impression on the QX (4b) it still places a tray there every other cycle or 3-4 cycles in a row.

Tool had bent pins at startup. Straightened them and started production around 8:20. Had a solid morning running spinach and 50/50. Spring mix was horrible. They didn't have enough product and had to stop at times waiting for it to come. Denester B is having some faults every now and then. Had an infeed safety guard issue with the chain and peg outfeed magnetic safety guard was loose. Tightened and it fixed it. Replaced the sensor cable for the hopper conveyor as it had an open/shorted wire. Ran 27 pallets today.

Came into the plant this morning for a 9am startup. Ended up having a longer delay due to a possible visit from the FDA. During the time that they were down I cleaned the lens on the SVS. Calibrated it and the image was a sin wave instead of a horizontal line meaning that something was causing the light to not have a clear image to the camera. I removed the housing on the side of the lens assembly and saw that some of the LED's were burnt out. Ordering a replacement.

CCW constantly in error. Found several hoppers with sticky product in them causing zero and hopper drive errors. When an error occurs it would just dump it immediately and it wouldn't care what hopper on the Triangle it fell into. I changed the MDI to sync and turned ManDumC to on and now it will clear the error only when an interlock signal is sent from the packer. I tried to run it with auto clear to help streamline production but the error signal will not be sent in that mode. Only in stop mode does it output ERRSIG1. When running 24 ct. the feed system struggles to keep up with CCW. After making these changes production was running well as it could. 98% eff.

Monitored production. For the Triangle to reject errors the CCW has to be in stop mode on error and manual dump confirm with it in sync mode. (Manual dump confirm doesn't have be on. If they want to zero the scale or drain it they can run it in clean out mode on the HMI for the Triangle) Had a meeting with plant management and told them that production will run a lot better with clean properly made product.

No production running today. Changed the CAL-PS and tested WH errors and the same problems occur. I also tested another scale and found the same issues. Troubleshot the camera and found that the camera and cable had some corrosion. I replaced it but it didn't work. I plugged the new camera directly from the RCU USB CTL Board P-5582-1 and it worked fine. Might have an issue with the USB connectors and or the ethernet cable. Metal strip for the Thomson drive was replaced. Had a call with Hiroshi Kisamira from IJ about further WH testing.
Came into the plant today with the FDA on site. Was told that they will contact me when production can continue. Cannot do any work on the production floor until FDA has given the all clear to Dole.

Came into plant after being notified that they have started production today. Still having occasional denester faults. Was going to make some modifications to the CCW by moving the UO4 PS to the opposite side of the main body but they're running on 2nd shift tonight.
Came on site with the FDA delaying production startup. No one is allowed on the floor during that time.
I was able to get permission to try to troubleshoot the CCW ethernet issues but didn't get anywhere with it.

Came on site with production running the best it's been on a morning startup. From 7/6 - 7/9 they were running at 98.6%. 23172 proper dumps, 239 unders, 2 overweights, 80 over scales. After the crew went on break I was testing the infeed camera and saw that it was causing the machine to lock up. It would still run production making proper combinations and the cursor on the screen would move when touched but none of the on screen tabs change. Turned off power to the CCW and opened the RCU and removed the Ethernet cable to the network extender and plugged it back in. Powered on the CCW and the camera works. (RCU software is W0171L 13.1) I moved the USB hub away from the PS-Feeder with no change. Updated RCU software to W0205F.

Production was running smoothly this morning. Camera is still not working but it isn't causing the RCU to freeze. I turned off the power to the CCW and moved the cable away from the noise filter and powered back on. Camera is working for the time being. Camera is still causing the RCU to freeze up. I have wound up the USB and Ethernet cables tighter with a ferrite core and the issue still happens.

Running 24ct and was having issues with double dumps. The CCW was running at 60wpm in stroke on demand while the Triangle was running at 20cpm. I placed the TH in pool and this fixed that issue. I also saw that the camera again was causing lockups. I managed to connect the camera via USB, solely, bypassing the network extender and couldn't reproduce the issue. I reconnected the network extender and couldn't reproduce the issues. Possible that I may need to order new parts for the camera unit. USB CTL Board, Network extenders, and camera.

Monitored production. Loaded older software (W0171) but was unable to get the camera working properly. Swapped the camera in the RCU with the infeed camera to see if it was hardware it loaded fine and will continue monitoring tomorrow.

Camera is still malfunctioning. Customer told me that it would be fine if it was unplugged and not used. They don't want the camera causing the CCW to lockup. I think the network extenders may be the culprit.

Validated all Ceia metal detectors. All metal detectors are using test samples of 1.5mm FE, NFE and 2.0SS. T/MS21 20900236083 wasn't picking up test samples while running links of gluten based hotdogs. Replaced the SCD board and did a TA auto learn by placing my thumb to the side of the middle of the receiver on the head. Auto learned the product by passing it several times and it worked. SE is 299, DM 4.

Came on site with the CCW in production. I saw that the speeds were set to high on C1 and C2. (100wpm) Slowed them down to 70wpm which helped efficiency-wise. Getting a lot of overweight errors on C1 due to WDU 7,8 being down. Target weight is 397g with an upper limit of 5g. I raised it to 10 to help reduce the amount of OW errors. Changed the OW count to 5 from 1 to reduce the amount of error stoppages. The TH on both sides while in production are not opening according the the drive pattern set. When I test drive it, it opens and closes properly. When I run it in production it will open about halfway and wait until the product is discharged from the WH then fully open then close fully then open halfway again. I have tried doing a debug initialize and updating the software to W0171 (not the newest but newer than the previous software W1080S) Tried running the filling machine slower and slowing down the CCW wpm to 60 and still has no effect on it. If I run it in drain it will act the same as production. The customer states that this hasn't happened before. They changed the WCU board and set the DIPSW's properly and it is the same board as the one they changed, revision number and all. After messing with the timings on the IS-TH1/2, I found that anything between 300-700ms causes the TH to work properly. However I have to be around 650ms for the product to cycle properly without jam-ups.

Came on site this morning with the maintenance manager putting AFV values back into the RCU. They stated that the TH wouldn't work and that the CCW couldn't power up on the RCU when touching the power key. I put the presets and machine settings back on to the RCU and tried to run production. The TH wouldn't operate properly and kept faulting out. I cycled power and when the main menu popped up the settings and presets were missing. I tried again putting them back in and saw that it wouldn't accept anything from the CF card. I checked the battery on the DMU and it was at 3.09 VDC (which is good). I loaded the previously installed software (backup) and it still was messing up. I changed the DMU and then did a debug initialize and the settings now save properly. The TH is still acting up. I removed it from the housing and watched it operate. It stops at the right location only because the mechanical stop causes it but then it looks as if it loses position. Changed the cam sensor board and it works properly. Started running production and the TH still require at leasts 650ms on the IS-TH1/2 delay for it to run smoothly. The CCW cleanly dumps from the TH 99% of the time. Sometimes a stray peanut or two will be caught up which causes no issues. The filler isn't getting all the product out of the DTH that it controls which is causing overs and underweights.

According to the plant manager the RCU screen showed up with a no data message popup upon power up. However all the settings were still in the system and presets. The TH again messed up last night. I had the maintenance password changed so no one could get into it to make changes. To get the TH working again I powered off the scale and removed J411 and J412 and reseated them and it worked fine. Voltages are good. I have +5.02V, +15.12V, -15.11V, +38.9V. I am reading +38.9V at the EXC board and I measured voltage while the TH were running and it was stable. I did some further testing of getting the TH to open and close properly. I removed the inputs and outputs from the relay board and then put the scale in drain with the IS-TH1/2 down to 0 and it still doesn't work properly. I removed the CF from the DMU and made a copy on my laptop. I formatted the CF and then place the contents back on it and I will see if there is anymore data issues. I have tried turning on DIPSW2-1 on to see if the TH act differently and it doesn't. I have moved the TH cables from J411 and J412 to J413 and J414 and it isn't any different. I have debug init again and then removed the DMU completely from the WCU and removed the battery. I've let it sit for 5-10 minutes and then put it back in and turned DIPSW3-3 to reset IP. It looked as if it was going to work when I put it into drain mode it cycled properly. I did a zero adjustment and it cycled properly. I put it into production by making a new preset (I didn't load anything into the RCU it is a clean slate. I ran production with the IS-TH1/2 at 0 and it continued to act up. Managed to get WDU8 working which has helped with Combinations. Adjusted the stop gap on it. WDU7&10 might have a bad load cell or DUC board.

Came into plant with all data erased. Scale was turned off last night and turned back on this morning. Tried to put values back in parameters and presets manually and the TH wouldn't work properly. I had to power down and do another debug initialize and I also moved the TH cables from J413 and J414 to J411 and J412. Once I did this the TH worked but it still acts up without having a delay in the IS-TH1/2 of at least 650ms. I tried loading the AFV values back in but they wouldn't load. Running production of 16oz peanuts at 70wpm and still having overweight issues. Recieved fresh DMU software and loaded it on a FAT formatted CF and loaded it on the DMU after doing a debug initialize, removing the DMU from the WCU, removing the CF card, and unplugging the battery. Waited 10 minutes and plugged in the battery, CF card, and DMU board. Did another debug initialize and cycled power and ran it in drain mode. In drain the TH no longer messes up, but in production is still does.

Memory was lost again this morning. According to the customer they didn't power down the equipment. I still think they did. Recap: The boards that have been changed are the TH boards, cam sensor in TH1, ADC, WCU, DMU, EXC. I have tried using fresh DMU software on a freshly formatted FAT CF card with no changes in production. I have done several debug initializes and complete removal of the DMU board with the battery removed. I have tried putting the TH cables into different ports. The problem remains the same. The TH will open part way when waiting for a combination then opens fully when found and then closes and then opens part way. I have put the original WCU board back in and the CCW runs fine but the TH still act up. Parts ordered for tomorrow. Customer needs to make changes to the filler system so it completely empties the contents from the TH into the jar. 75% of the time there is leftover product that gets filled into the next jar which is the main cause of over/unders. After playing with the timings in the IS-WH delay, if it is set to 300ms or more it will cause the TH to operate properly when a combination is made every cycle. If it misses a cycle then the TH props halfway open.

Came in this morning and the memory held but the scale was probably left on overnight. Parts arrived and I changed the RCU board first then the WCU, EXC, Relay with no change. Ended up coming down to the linkages on the TH weren't straight as they should be. 8 - 9 o'clock is what the TH drive arm should look like connected to the TH. Put the orignal WCU,EXC, and Relay board back in. Leaving the RCU in tonight and seeing if the memory retains.

Came in this morning and memory was lost again. On the screen it showed up AFV errors asking me to zero heads 1-4. Customer requested that I replace the RCU board since it didn't help ($3500 part they didn't want around) I put in the new WCU board in hopes that it will retain it's AFV values. The TH began to act up again and a HDRV initialize cleared the fault. Production is running 398g of peanuts @120jpm. Couldn't solve the issue due to the customer stating that they would take care of the memory loss problem.
Supervised and monitored the line for stoppages for a downtime report. Completed 33.5 pallets. Worked on the denesters after production to allow them to denest properly.
Continued downtime reports. At completion of production we completed 34 pallets.
Continued downtime reports. Best day yet. Completed 40 pallets with an average tpm of 50.7.

Came into the plant with the CCW fixed by the maintenance team. I had a discussion with my contact about what they had done to fix it. They told me that they had changed the TH DU board and they said that it usually fixes it but it didn't. They also changed the EXC board and the stepper motor and it didn't fix anything. The TH would open and close sporadically. They had then changed the cam sensor board and it would work but required them to turn the shaft completely counter clockwise then tighten the linkage on the shaft and it has worked with no issues since then. They have had issues with the TH DU board and cam sensor boards going out often. They have at least changed those boards 3 times, if not more. I have asked them to put a ground wire connected to the bolt that secures the TH board assemblies to the metal frame of the secured nitrogen chamber in hopes that if there is a static build up inside that the ground wire can give more protection. They had also asked if there is any other TH systems that they could use if this doesn't fix the issue. I had mentioned a pneumatic system but they would have to go through Gary Tobin for that revision.

Travel. Weigh conveyor pulse error occurs on attempted startup. I tried swapping the drivers with no change. I put a new PCU board and it worked fine. Customer wanted me to check to make sure the rejector output works and it does. The conveyor was running backwards because the customer had the jumper plugged in for a direction change. I removed it and it works properly. I ran static weights across the conveyor and it was stable.
Travel, picked up Haider from the airport.
Powered up CCW-R. Installed lastest RCU software. Found that the 260E FB has the wrong solenoid and photo eye voltage (24VDC) They require controls of 115VAC. Parts will be in tomorrow.

Changed accel and decel times on 90E from ten second to .6 and 1 accordingly. Ran product on the whole system. CCW-M is having an issue with the DF not vibrating strongly when tightened to the support. If it is slightly loose it vibrates strongly. Possible something broke off of the DF pan.

Production is starting late due to upstream equipment not working properly. Had Bama order a new threaded rod for delievery tomorrow to fix the DF vibration but it has a lead time of up to a month. I had a maintenance person weld the thread to the rod and placed it back onto the DF and it works well. Ran 20ct biscuits the whole day and didn't have any issues. Went over the differences with a CCW-R and M with the production lead.
Monitored production. They ran at max production and the line handles it very well.

Arrived on site and found the weigher able to power up and test drive. Did further testing and found that the communication cable from the hub going to the DUC on WDU#14 was bad causing the voltage to drop for the whole weigher causing a WCU-DCU communication error. They have purchased a new scale and are planning on having it installed labor day weekend so it isn't necesary to spend a lot of time trying to get the scale to 100%. I plan on leaving the communications cable to WDU#14 unplugged and taped up so they can run it. Tested span weight production and had no issues. The only things that don't work are WDU#14, BH 5, and WH3(BH open doesn't operate) zero and spanned scale and did a repeatability test.
Came on site and tested scale. Zeroed and drained.

Word was not passed on that the scale was able to run production so it wasn't cleaned or setup. They said they would have it clean by 1130. By that time they had changed their minds and requested that I be here for startup Monday morning around 0500.

Came on site feeling ill, rested for several hours and I felt better. Came on site to see that they tried to run production on the CCW but they never set the Triangle Wheel up to run to the CCW sat there waiting for an interlock signal. Ran 48g of beef per side @60wpm

Nestlé installed the CCW-R on their own. They made mistakes due to service not being on site. The drain holes were plugged up by covering one and having main power routed through the other. When they routed main power they opened the hole larger for the flex cable to fit. They don't have anymore flex cable to have it properly installed so they knocked out a hole in the same area on the back side of the body so that water could drain out. They are trying to find an elbow pipe so it can drain because the adapter for the drain plugs are in the way of the mezzanine support bars. The RCU cables are ran through ridged pipe connecting directly under the scale cabinet which they also knocked out. I advised them that the ridged pipe will transfer vibration but AFV should help but would rather avoid it if possible. I also told them we have holes just for routing cables for power, RCU, interlocks, etc. L11, L31 is only reading 238VAC. Should be 480VAC. RCU bracket hasn't been changed. They used the one from the NZ. The RCU has no adjustment for angle until they put the proper one on. RCU camera wasn't installed but there is no need since the RCU is up on the mezzanine and the frame of the mezzanine is in the way of the camera. Conducted maintenance training and went over all the screens in the RCU. I/O testing was good and ready for production tomorrow.
Ran production of 40g of chicken (stripped, frozen) at 70wpm per side. Did operator training for several operators.
Trained more operators and maintenance staff. Ran production of 48g of frozen sliced chicken.

Travel to Augusta, GA. Rental agency didn't have a car so I went to another location with them closing early. I went to the airport to get a vehicle and got one. Came on site with the Atlas broken down to the shafts. Replaced the Schmidt couplings and rebuilt the rear jaw assembly. This took a lot of time to replace the couplings.
Completed the front jaw assembly but found that the cams don't meet up  for the jaw alignment. Replaced the rear and front jaw assemblies and swapped the cams.
Completed the jaw assemblies and did a jaw alignment. The jaws align but there is no D-motion and the bags were getting torn. Removed the jaw assemblies again to swap cams again.

Called Luis Rivera about the cams. Found that the cams may belong to a right side drive unit. After attempting again to rebuilt the jaw assemblies I tried to swap the cams but turn them 180 degrees and flip them left to right. By doing this I was able to confirm that the cams will work when I get the proper cams with the countersunks and dowel pin cutout sent in.

Confirmed from Jim Tate that the cams belonged to a right side drive unit, Kellogg's has a left side drive unit. Cams have been removed from an ATLAS in California to be sent overnight. Did a further overview of the ATLAS and found that the back seal forward solenoid was always applying air pressure to the back seal against the former. After further review I found that the Y6/7 knife fire solenoid was connected to the Y5 back seal 15 solenoid. I swapped the airlines and connectors and it properly works for the knives and forward motion for the back seal 15 forward motion.

Cams arrived rebuilt entire jaw assembly. Ran some bags but the knife wasn't firing. I looked into the system config and changed the knife solenoid type from 1 to 0 and then it worked. Had a heater or sensor error on startup. It was a snagged cable which caused the issue. Reseated cable and it worked fine. Ran several bags at 140 BPM.

Came into plant with the ATLAS and air turned off. Customer was stating that they had some issues with the knife not firing. Turned on ATLAS and air and tested some bags. Had to redo the knife fire for 1 and 2 (proximity sensor) as it was firing incorrectly. Ran production for several hours with no issues until later in the evening when the knife was sticking against the top of the jaw causing it to not retract. Had to adjust the jaw to allow it unrestricted movement.

Cam follower cover was jammed against the cam cover causing the jaw to not seal properly. Greased cams and fixed the cover. Recommending they replace the covers for the cam and order some cam follower covers. After looking at the air diagram for in/out knives it shows that it is a single solenoid instead of a double. Found a spare single solenoid and installed it and it works properly from the RCU and while in production, one bag, etc. Met with Felipe and discussed issues and what was resolved and still outstanding. Travel home for doctors appointment.

Ran several bags of pretzel nuggets at .7, 3, 4, 5, 6, 24, 28oz. At 135, 115, 115, 115, 115, 70 wpm and 115 for double dump and 70 wpm for single dump of 28oz respectively. I did both dumps in case they have a hard time keeping steady product on top of the feeders. Ran very well but they may need some type of product control such as a crash tube or some standoff type guides to keep product from swirling in the transition chute.

Validated both Ceia's. 1.5mm FE, NFE, and 2.0mm SS(316). Filled out both reports and gave a copy to Angie Floyd. They need a list of parts for the Ceia's for spares. They are inquiring about getting Cognex cameras to read the barcodes instead of using Accusort barcode scanners.

Production assistance for running 21oz pouch of chipotle cashews and almonds. Running at 75WPM per side. Saw issues with stability for the heads. Found that the stable time was set to 510ms with a stable count of 4. Changed to 600ms and 3 count and the weights are better. It would dump 600g but weight slightly less than 21oz before the changes. Vibratory conveyor had a pan that helps center product on the DF and that pan is resting on the CCW which transfers vibration resulting in unstable heads and weights. The mezzanine shakes as well when the conveyor is on. Isolation pads are helping but only do so much. At the end of the day the weights were good but would like to have the vibration issues taken care of. C1/C2 99.9/98.9% eff.
Meeting with Kraft R&D. Went over the results for yesterday's run and what is needed for optimum production.

Came on site with the DACS not running production properly but the belts were working. Loaded software for the new load cell that the customer installed and now it is able to run. The weights are off and I tried spanning it with no luck. I removed the load cell assembly and reset it. Now it works. Ran 2289g of coffee beans and compared it with the table scale and they were within +/- 1g.

Was told to return to site because some presets weren't working. Upon arrival I saw that it was running in conveyor mode. I turned conveyor mode off and ran production and saw no issues. Came on site with the CCW powered up. Tried zeroing in sync mode but it wouldn't do it (Bagger was ready and sending signal). Turned to self and it worked. Checked relay board and saw 20,21 input LED flash from bagger running. Turned on manual dump confirm and 28,29 didn't light the output LED. Checked voltage on Relay-PS and it was at 20.4VDC. (Supposed to be +5VDC!!!!!!!!!!!) Replaced it with a similar Allen Bradley 110VAC input / 24-28VDC output PS.(This is wrong 100VAC in and +5VDC out!!!!!!) Now the relays fire and production can run. Put span weights on WH and tested CC. They all work but the Feeders are not vibrating. Checked voltages. Found wire 9&10 from KM3 not on XT603. Each wire was wire nutted and two other wires were terminated but were connected to nothing. Removed those wires and terminated the proper wires (0V and 200V). Ran in drain and tested all hoppers and RF's. RF1,13 not vibrating. Fuses are good, customer changed both FDRV boards prior to me arriving. May need new coils or adjustment on the plate and coil. Had Tyson order 2 RF coils and a PS-Relay. Ran 2265g of sausage toppings at 60 BPM with 98.5% eff.

Replaced PS-Relay with an Ishida  approved one and one coil. Put CCW in drain and found that both cables for 1 and 13 are bad. I swapped RF 1 with 2 and 12 with 13 and 1 and 13 worked fine while 2 and 12 weren't. Having Tyson order cables for them to install at a later time.

Came on site with them running production of 16oz trays of spring mix. Observing production it looked fine. About an hour later they began having problems. They had a M329 motion controller not ok error with the fault code of 25674 on the carriage. I cleared the faults and did a dry cycle run to see when the error occurs. It occurred when the tamps would come down it would hit the carriage moving it slightly forward causing the overrun sensor to illuminate. Looking at the tamps as they would go into the carriage hoppers it wasn't even by any means. The tamps would hit the inside edge and would slightly bend the tamps as it rubbed against the carriage hopper. I checked the carriage offset and changed the value from 31mm to 39mm after doing a manual adjustment to center the tamps in the carriage. Once that was done it worked flawlessly. Continued running production of 16oz spring mix.

Some of the issues I was having was trying to get the offset for the carriage changed. I would change it and then do a re-home but it would look as if it wouldn't move the carriage back further at all. I changed the offset to 100 and it didn't budge any further back to be centered below the HTH's. I need a explanation of how to properly do an offset change as I "lucked out" with finally getting it to center. I also noted that when the carriage was hitting the overrun sensor on the forward side (tamping area) I couldn't reverse the carriage jog by holding both the stop and reset buttons while pressing Carriage Rev on the HMI. I could only move it when I unplugged the cable from the overrun sensor. Then I was able to reverse it. I then plugged it back in and double checked that the sensor would work. Also, what is a proper password to use to get full access. I used username TECH password FRESH123 and that gave me access. Didn't know if there is an Ishida one that will be standard for when more units are made.

I firmly believe that the sensors have been fiddled with. It's highly unusual for needing an 8mm adjustment for the carriage offset. I will try to test the jog issue and overrun sensor when I have time with the machine.

Startup this morning seems to require a little bit of resetting reject chutes and door switches by opening and closing them several times till it allows it to reset. I think they should try to dry off the DS as much as possible as moisture can slightly affect the door guards operation. The white C shaped UHMW door holder with the springs on guard door 5 isn't allowing the door to close unless you push one of the springs open then shut the door. Might need a replacement piece sent but I will try to fiddle with it. The reject chute was left in the reject position which when doing a re-home was still staying out in the reject position while everything else homed. I couldn't run production because it was left like that. Had to force the output on the HMI to return it back then I was able to run. They may have put it in drain and then left it like that this morning and I didn't notice it on the HMI.

I did find that the compartments on the DS (not the control panel with the PLC and drivers) that contain the servo motors for the tamp/swing, and carriage have standing water in them. I dried it out with some paper towels. It maybe a good idea to have two holes knocked out for these compartments. One for positive air, the other for it to drain out. Similar to we force water/moisture out of the CCW. I would suggest to knock out a hole on the side for incoming air because water won't pool around the plug and of course a drain hole on the bottom. (Did this with the J-Box at Dole)

Started production of spinach and had product dumping without a tray underneath. Found that the reflector for the tray sensor was wet and was causing that problem. They have been running very well for a little under 2 hours this morning.

Another suggestion is having a small incline on the bottom tray guide rails towards the end by the servo tamp section. I think a small incline (maybe a 1-2 degree adjustment) in the red circled area will help with the momentum from accel/decel moving the trays forward which can cause crashes, damage the tray, and spill product. I do see at the end the bottom guide there is a bend that could also be bent slightly in the opposite direction to have the end of the tray more level or tilted to prevent excessive movement after decel. I did make a change to the decel setting. It was at 400mm/sec/sec but changed it to 380. I do want to try to avoid making changes on settings unless they warrant it. I do not want to make FX feel as if they need to always mess with the settings.

After several hours production has been running steadily with some hiccups from inexperienced staffing. They had slowed the CCW down to 25wpm at first, then turned it to 40wpm. I placed some wire ties on the bottom tray guide rail which created a speed bump that slowed down the momentum of the tray without the tray riding up from it and crashing. The second shift crew is more experienced and are running at 60wpm. Since the zip-ties have been fastened it has worked near flawless at keeping trays from sliding. If it does slide it's only a 1/4 of what it used to. Energy chains for the tamp and carriage are broken.

Had no major issues with startup. Some sensors needed to be dried but once that was done it was running smoothly. Running 16oz of spinach with a reduced crew so the CCW is only running at 30wpm. Changeover to 11oz spinach. Removed 16oz carriage and put in the 11oz one and tried to start production but had an error show up on the HMI. It read, dipping chute not up. I looked at the dipping funnel sensor and it was lit. I unplugged the sensor and reapplied it and it still had the error pop up. I physically moved the carriage up and down and the sensor would turn on and off but also noticed that the bracket that the sensor sees was contorted. Removed the carriage and I straightened it out. Once that was done it ran with no issues. Made adjustments to the door latch on guard door 5. It closes smoothly.

Travel. Traffic and rental car wobbling resulted in increased travel time. Arrived on site with the DS not running due to less demand for trays. Did some testing with holding down the stop button and pressing the jog reverse or forward button on the HMI when the over run sensor is made. It worked on the forward end but didn't on the reverse end (home) on the carriage. Found when it would make the over run on the return end it would also hit the internal limit sensor at or around the same time. We moved the sensor bracket on the (home) return end and that now works accordingly. Found that when the internal limit sensor was activated we couldn't move the carriage at all. We had first removed the countersunk bolts holding the motor for the carriage to loosen the belt to allow the carriage gear to spin freely and move the carriage from the sensor and would put it all back together but also found that when you hit reset and then press stop and tap on the reverse or forward button on the HMI and do it repeatedly, it would move the motor little by little until it would finally no longer be sensing the internal limit sensor. (Didn't always work at times when testing) When we moved the sensor bracket on the (home) return end we also had to adjust the origin offset for the carriage from 39mm to 54.5mm. Ran in dry cycle without a problem. This sounds exactly like the issues explained to me about the carriage faults so hopefully this will take care of the problems.

Monitored production of 16oz spinach. Haven't had any issues with the DS today. Worked on the 11oz carriage. The bracket for the dipping chute was bent enough that it was causing issues with the sensor not being made. Took the bracket off and straightened it out. Tomorrow is an off day for production on the line so we will conduct tests on the line then. Returned Mike Kelly's rental car at the airport to conserve expenses.

Production wasn't scheduled to run but they had problems on another line so they tried to start up on the DS. They had issues with trying to get it started. They tried to zero adjust the CCW after they had started production on the DS. They need to put the DS in drain mode so it rejects any manual dump prior to starting production on the DS. Once the CCW is zeroed and calling for product then they need to put the DS in production.

Tried to run production but had clutch faults on one of the tamps. After manually opening and closing the carriage hoppers we saw that the hopper on one side was struggling to fully open. We removed the 16oz carriage and saw that the bracket for the dipping chute sensor was badly bent and straightened it. Also found that the cylinder on one side was difficult to manually open the hopper doors while the other was with ease. Opened the set screw on the bottom side of the cylinder to allow less cushion to open it more freely. Once that was done we placed the carriage back onto the dipping chute and tested it in dry cycle with no problems. By the time we finished line 14 was running.

Tested out over run sensors on the tamp and carriage. On the carriage we had problems when the over run sensor on the index/tamping end wasn't allowing us to hit the reset button then press and hold the stop button while pressing Jog REV. The only way around it was to unplug the over run sensor on that side. We then hit reset and held down stop while pressing Jog REV. Plugged the sensor back in. On the home/return end of the carriage we had the same problem but were able to move it using the HMI but had to have one person pressing the reset button frequently while the other was pressing stop and Jog FWD. After around 5-10 tries, it was free from that over run sensor.
On the tamps when the over run sensor is made we are able to hit the reset button then press and hold stop while pressing Jog Down on the HMI.

Had another issue with FX trying to clear a fault. Went out to the floor and found it was the swing chute over run on the index side was tripped. We had no issue holding down the stop button and pressing Jog REV to unblock the over run sensor. Did find that the sensor bracket was moved. There was a mark on the bracket indicating where the center of the sensor should be. Moved the over run sensor back further to give some wiggle room for the swing chute because when the bracket is in the home position it was very close to the over run sensor. Tested jogging the carriage to the over run and was able to use the HMI to move it away from the over run sensor. Ran in dry cycle with no issues.

Had a meeting with FX maintenance and management about their issues with the DS. Provided them with some manuals and troubleshooting techniques. Showed two maintenance personnel (Wayne and Ralph) how to clear errors created by the over run sensors being flagged. They both seemed relieved to know how to do this. Need to get some cord grips and air fittings plus air lines to force air into the carriage servo compartment as that always has a pool of water in it every morning due to condensation.

Startup this morning had a small issues which Fresh Express handled. A clutch fault was reoccurring and found out they had replaced the tamp bar without drilling holes for the I-dent ball spring to rest in. They just need to drill a small concave hole for that ball to rest in until a great amount of force is applied to it so it can slip without bending the tamper bar or the support bracket connected to the Thomson drive. Went over how to clear over run sensor errors with 2 maintenance staff. Explained the proper procedures and had them clear the errors.

Assisting production after scale was relocated within the plant. Found that the infeed for C1 and C2 were not going to there respective sides. The CCW was installed 90 degrees off. Wreck on I-77S which delayed travel to plant. Arrived on site with the gripper arms issue being from the settings being erased for that specific setting. Dole maintenance said they have checked out the tool and found nothing wrong with it. 1a, 3a, and 2b had /!\ on them. I removed the tool and had them clean the pins and blowout any water that could have been inside the service unit clamp. I checked Relay Board 1 and TB3 pins 1, 2+3 with no issues with continuity from there to the female connectors on the service unit clamp. Took the tool into the maintenance shop and found that the red wire for the thermocouple was disconnected on 1a. Also found that the grounding clip was broken on it as well. I reconnected both of those wires and put the tool back together and tested it out on the floor. Had no issues with temperatures fluctuating and 1a now reads the proper temperature. It was a solid zero before. Ran the QX1100 in empty operation mode with no issues. Will have Dole clean the pins and blowout any water whenever they remove the tool from now on.

Found the Thompson drive that needs to be sent to Sweden and have labelled it to be sent back. Changed the WH drive parameters for 1, 2, and 3 according to how it was tested in Japan for the WH errors. I will try to find time to test to see if they still occur but may be unable to find the time with their production schedule. Replaced the SVS LED but having issues with trying to get it to work with production. I have calibrated it but when I turn on the use seal camera function it gives me a 1020 error. (Johnny could you explain this one to me please?)

Dole has ordered 2 M8/NC 8mm NPN (IE P# 483-3673) proximity sensors for the tamp clutch. They currently have them jumped out in the DS control panel. The tamper bracket on lane B is broken on the side closest to the QX. They are currently tamping 3 instead of 4 trays at a time until this is fixed. If they don't have the part readily available then I will have them order one or see if Bessemer City Machine Shop has that bracket in their CNC machine still. Production started up around 8am due to an extended sanitation. Production started up with no issues. The bracket that was discussed yesterday was actually the tamper bars that were bent. I heard that only one tamper was bent but what I found out was that all but one were bent. I straightened out the bars and they are ready to be installed. Sensors for the tamp clutch have come in and I will install them during a changeover if time permits. Haven't seen any WH errors or issues since changing the drive parameters. Tried to get the seal checker working but haven't had any luck with communication between the RCU SC and the HMI CS. Running 6oz of spinach decently.

Sometime around noon they were having a diffucult time running production with the DS and the QX having issues. The DS issue was from the ball spring plungers on a tamp that were completely loose causing the clutch fault sensor to activate on the way up to home position which would emergency stop the DS. The QX had gripper in/out servo alarms. I checked the belt that is responsible for the in/out motion and it was stuck because it couldn't travel any further. I popped it loose and reset the QX. It locked again. I looked at the offset and it was set to 36mm. I changed it to 32mm and started the QX in production and waited till the gripper arms were at home + offset then opened the guard door to stop it. Then closed the door and manually controlled the tool and raised it up to see if the gripper arms would get hit by the tool which it didn't.

Installed a new sensor and cable for the clutch fault sensors on Lane B downstream side. Tested it and it works fine. Had to adjust some origin offsets for the Tamp on Lane A (0mm) and the Carriage on Lane B (6mm) Dry cycled the QX and the DS with no issues. Tested WH errors. Had several dumps of actual product dropping from 4-5WH's with zero WH errors. I had turned the BH's off to force the WH's to dump at once. Stagger was at 0. Still no success with communicating with the seal vision system for the Camsensor. Production with be starting again at 700am tomorrow morning.

Startup was around 7:30. They hadn't planned on running 16 today according to their schedule but line 17 was down. QX had some issues with product caught in tool errors. Tried changing the lane tray stop position because the trays kept hitting the edge of the bone plate but it didn't adjust. Cycled power and it still wouldn't change. Looked at the carriage move stroke and it was set to 1135mm. I changed it to 1145mm and that fixed it.

CCW has P2706B which is the default (original) software for it. WH errors when dumping more than 4 WH's to discharge product are nonexistent. Drive parameters for each setting for the WH have fixed it.

SVS is still not communicating to the RCU to tell it when there is product outside of the seal but it does show it on the Camsensor HMI clearly. Customer has no intention of fully utilizing it since they have laborers on the line that can visibly spot badly sealed trays so they can remove them. Ethernet cable that connects to the plants switch is unplugged because in the past it has brought the SVS internal network down.

Made a spreadsheet containing all the settings for the QX1100 in case they lose them or the backup. The line has been running well with the exception of 1a impression turned off as the knife needs to be checked out. Could be a bad spring or dull knife.

Travel. CCW powers up with a DUC network error at times. When I press the power key on the RCU QF5 and QF2 trip which turns off power to the CCW. Found that by removing the fuse board cables 601 and 602 that it won't cause the breaker to trip. Plugged in 601 and it didn't trip. Plugged in 602 and it did. I moved on to the FDRV board 1 and removed the RF cables to 5,6,7,8 and hit the power key and had no issue with breakers tripping. I plugged in 5,6,7, then 8 tripped the breaker. RF Coil is the culprit because I plugged RF8 cable into 7 and had no issues. RF coil is being ordered and will be installed by the plant.

DUC network errors became an issue. I had removed all the +5VDC comm cables to each DUC and plugged them in one by one until the error occurred. DUC 12 was bringing down the voltage and was replaced. Once I tried running in drain mode I began to have more  DUC network errors. I had removed 6,8,9,10,11,13,14 and was able to get around seeing as they had no spare HUB board. Did find that the Scale  along side it had a different board number (5535 compared to 5425) but installed it and it fixed the DUC network errors. During production on C1 sometimes it no longer receives an output from the packer to dump product and will sit idle. Arrived on site with the customer not yet ready to install the new CCW-R. Instead we worked on a CCW-NZ-216B-D that had some issues. Replaced all the RF cables. RF 3 works now but RF 13 still isn't vibrating. Checked fuse and it's good Coil is good as I plugged it into RF 14 on FDRV. Boards came in and I replaced the FDRV board and RF 13 still doesn't work. Tried swapping WDU 13 and 14 to see if the DUC board was the problem which it wasn't. Found that on the AC fuse board on wire 13 from XT to the connector on pin 1 has no continuity. Removed AC fuse board and found that it was burned open on the back side of the board. Found on WDU #7 that the DDU board had a broken EEPROM that was the problem. Replaced it and it now works properly.

CCW-RZ unable to run production. Packer sends output signal to the relay board but the relay board doesn't output a discharge confirm. Ran 5lbs of pizza topping (sausage) at 99.5% eff.

RF's and DF do not vibrate but the hoppers open/close during production. Checked 200V,0V which were good. Fuses good. No 200V on KM2-5. Found that F603 had a severed connection on the fuse output going to KM2-5. Water ingress has been the issue with all of the service calls lately as the CCW is not sealed securely. Running 283g of crackers. Good efficiencies averaging 99.1%. Had some PH errors on 7 (56106) due to the infeed adjustment pan not being large enough to catch the product falling from the fastback. They use a tumble drum system without running it (they have no need for seasoning before it goes onto the scale) and it's not centered over the DF. (it would be if it was running) They have locally made a pan that can keep product from landing on the RF and slide it to the DF centered.
There is no weight reading on WH14. May need a new load cell / DUC board.
Trained 3rd shift supervisor and CI engineer on CCW production screens. Travel home.

F-SPA running at 60BPM. Customer wants 70-80. Brush unit had a loose set screw on the timing pulley causing the top brush to stop moving and holding the bag tight for the bag gripper to grip it evenly. Adjusted the gap between the brush rollers to allow bigger bags to get in. Drop conveyor had to excessive movement causing the bags entering the conveyor after it drops then returns and rocks the bags which resulted in the bag not being gripped properly causing a crash. Found linkage and eye bolt worn badly. Replaced it and now the drop conveyor is smooth in motion. Lubed bearing and shafts which took the squealing noise away. (07/12453 model) tested bags at different speeds and found that 60bpm is the most efficient with pork rind bags.

Heavy traffic in the morning. Late start on production which didn't start till past 10. Running pork rinds at 60bpm. Product in bag doesn't settle well at all making it hard for the F-SPA to seal bags to strip. Customer changed settings on bagger to allow product to settle better which helped a lot. Had to make mechanical adjustments to the brush rollers and drop conveyor linkage. (10/10480 model)
DC 24V down means door isn't shut closed all the way.

Travel. Arrived at plant and installed new CW-CAL software(P2881A ver2.1) Had to change IP addresses to default to install the software. Once software was loaded changed back to Tyson's IP addresses:
Powered on and checked to make sure communication is good between RCU and main body. Searched for the parts that were sent to modify the CCW's. Found the parts and will install tomorrow.
Installed new drive arms for the WH's, replaced ring gate support bars, brackets, and RFT's. Still have 6 that are broken.

Threaded rod for the DF on one scale is broken and the other is missing. Cut a threaded rod to 4" and put nylon and a normal nut on the top and bottom side to match the dimensions of the threaded rod to support the DF. (1" thread showing on the top and bottom)  Removed the photo eyes for both scales as they have no use, were not used, and were damaged anyways. UHMW rollers need to be modified to allow the DF to spin without drastically throwing the weight off and rub against the rollers which could overload the motor and or break the rods on the RFT's. The UHMW rollers need to have the diameter reduced by 4mm on the bottom off the reduced diameter above the base resting on the RFT (38mm diameter is the bottom of the roller resting on the RFT, the bottom of the reduced part is 32mm) 13mm high to allow the DF to spin without hitting the rollers. Called the local fabrication shop and they will work on it tomorrow morning.

Had the rollers modified. Installed the rollers but they have some rubbing but should be fine as the roller also spins when the DF does rub against it. (The DF doesn't rub against certain rollers all the time) Weigh fluctuates slightly while running (drain mode) but with a load on it, it stabilizes better.  WH1 wouldn't open and would make a grinding noise. Found that the drive arm was pushed up to hard and caused that issue. Dropped the drive arm slightly and now it opens correctly and cleanly. Opened both scale tops and checked for any water ingress and found none. While the top was off I also checked to see if the DF bracket was loose as this has been an issue in the past and it was tight for both. Finished installing the infeed chute over the DF. Sanitation was still cleaning on arrival. Had to wait until they cleaned off the mezzanine to look at a CCW-R and CCW-M. CCW-R on WDU#1 had a grinding noise on the PH. Removed the drive and found that the spring and its assembly were not connected to the body of the drive. The cam sensor and flag were in pieces. Waiting for production to start. Delayed several times. Tested other equipment but not the CCW's. Will startup tomorrow in the morning.

Delayed startup. Production started at 1215. Running 10lbs (2 dumps) of chicken leg meat. Weights have been good. Software isn't discharging overscale errors properly. If 3 heads overscale then it's supposed to wait until after the second dump to then discharge the error all at once. It will not auto clear any overscale. It requires you to stop production then the error screen appears. It discharges the overscaled heads but it doesn't do them all at once and then send a manual dump signal after the last errored head dumps. Awaiting the software control card with detailed instructions.

Read the software control card and saw nothing on any settings that needs to be turned on for the overscales to be auto dumped. Found that the overscale can't be auto cleared because it is a load cell out of range overscale. Found that the software works properly when it is a target weight + upper limit weight. Will have to send the information off to IJ for them to work on it. Ran production of 10lbs of fresh chicken legs.
DACS-G and RE-G on line with power installed. 118VAC incoming power. Ran 454g of pasta 145mm length at 60m/min. Checked outputs for metal detect and underweight signal and the signal output is good.

Advised customer to not use the 24VDC power source for energizing coils to their counting system. Filled out installation report. Tested 340g and 454g packages for rejection at 50m/min. 250ms reject on time 300ms delay for left rejector and 600ms delay for right rejector. Suffered a head injury while on site from hitting my head on a metal cylindrical run off shoot.

Deep level initialized the DACS-G. Manually inputted all the presets and tested out running cases. They were running new products and needed to adjust and create new presets. Found that when new software was installed it may not have been fully initialized properly and also had the presets from the older software placed back onto the DACS which could have caused some corruption in the software.

Production began and had issues with certain labels not being read by the barcode reader. All the labels that had issues had the barcode closest to the edge or it was printed on the left side of the label. The ones on the right side didn't have any issues. Made adjustments to the guides on the infeed going into the X-ray which helped move the boxes away from the barcode reader which gave it less time to scan the box which is good so that it doesn't cause a NoRead2 error. Turned the barcode reader closer to the center of the boxes coming onto the DACS so it picks up the barcode faster. After making these changes the NoRead errors have diminished drastically. Monitored the data being sent from the barcode reader to the DACS to see if it is sending the wrong information but it was correct in every case. The reasons for NoRead errors is label placement, damaged labels, double barcodes from used boxes.

Input the rest of the presets into the DACS. Tested the new barcode on the IX-GA. Had to change the barcode length to 6 on the barcode reader and also in the preset. Changes that need to be made in the IX-GA to have the new barcodes working is changing the barcode length to 6 and adding two spaces after the number. Ex., 0002  | (| is the blinking cursor showing that there is two spaces after that number)

Found a lot of metal shavings inside the cabinets of the scale. Had to vacuum out shavings to prevent damage to the boards. Continued testing of interfaces. Tested Fastback photo eyes to shut off incline conveyor and pushed on DF to stop Fastbacks. Placed an object on the conveyor and it moved properly. Ran 112g carrots beans mix, 78g carrots soy mix. Product has melted which has led to some weight issues and missed cycles but it is working well.

Came in to conduct training but several crew members were obligated to be elsewhere. No training was conducted but was able to leave helpful hints in the instruction manuals for later use.
Trained several maintenance personnel, an operator, and a sanitation worker during the first shift. Trained more sanitation and maintenance workers in the third shift.

Went over install checklists and had PSD signed. Made backups of presets and machine settings. CCW runs in slave mode only. Manual Dump Confirm is on and Manual Dump Initiate is set to sync. The KleenLine depositor below sends an interlock signal (20,21) every time it does a full cycle (full revolution of movement) Currently if we drain the CCW of product it will do so if the depositor is running below. If it isn't running it will wait until the depositor is running. It will also send a dump confirm signal every cycle as well but only when the interlock signal is first sent. The important thing is to have the depositor in drain mode before the CCW starts to drain. The reason is because the if the depositor isn't ready to discharge the product sent to it will cause a mess and require time to clean it out. Currently the discharge signal sent to the depositor only works in production mode but I have spoken with Rich from KleenLine and he is working on changing the software to cause the depositor to discharge products every time a discharge signal is sent.

Talked to Thomas Zwann about DACS software and was told that there is software that needs to be installed prior to installing the new barcode software. He sent me the .zip file containing the .pdf files to install them properly.

NoRead1 errors on IX-GA for barcodes 0653 and 0708. It seems to catch the barcode at the end or near the end of the scan resulting in not being able to read it sometimes. Other barcodes stop scanning before it gets to the middle of the barcode.

Production started with some underweight issues. Boxes weighed by the DACS have up to a 225g difference compared to a table top scale. The weigh table length is physically 650mm long but in the setting it has to be 800mm for it to weigh properly. The box hangs off the end of the belt quite a bit and it is touching the conveyor right as the weight information is being processed and completed which throws off the weight by 200g. I raised the weight conveyor up about 10mm on each side and leveled it. It no longer hits the conveyor belt upon leaving the weigh conveyor which now weighs within 25-35g or so which is normal for speed of 47m/min on a case weigher. Having a lot of zero errors due to the huge fan up top in the warehouse. Once they turned down the fan the zero errors went away. The photo eye bracket for the barcode reader is broken and held on by tape. Over time the photo eye drifts and causes NoRead errors on the DACS. About 1600 the line was being jammed due to the IX-GA inspection conveyor wasn't turning well at all. Removed the conveyor and spun the gear on it by hand and it wasn't binding or tight feeling. I was able to turn the gear on the coupling freely and it was tight then loose. I removed the motor and the shaft was marred badly along with the coupling. Adjusted the preset weights for several presets. That way they can tell if a bag is missing in the case. Running 1150g of Famous Amos cookies @22bpm/35wpm (S.O.D.) 99.5% efficiency. Customer thought that issues of empty bags was because of the CCW. Reset histogram totals and after 100 cycles the CCW had 100% efficiency and there was several empty bags. Each time the CCW was sent an interlock it would dump product. Found that the packing machine wasn't sending the interlock at times due to mechanical timing issues. Each time that we viewed the bits on the PLC program it wouldn't complete the entire process to sent the output to dump which resulted in empty bags.

Had several issues with the packer but once that was fixed we had double dump issues when the CCW was at low product. Worked with their controls engineer to get it to cooperate. Running S.O.D. and the packer was pulsing the interlock signal extremely fast which caused some hiccups with the scale double dumping. I had the output from the CCW (DCS) in series with the output of the packer (Interlock in the PLC program) so that when I had product ready it would let the packer know it's ok to output the interlock signal. While in low product the interlock won't work until it is out of low product and a combination is made which in turn notifies the packer that it can initiate a interlock output.

Trying to figure out the interface for the case line with the CCW. There are 2 independent lines that each will be fed from a DTH and has 5 wires needing to go to the CCW for each. Production started at 700. Barcodes are placed on boxes improperly which causes the scanner to not read all the lines because of the angle. The new barcodes are a lot larger than the previous ones which makes it even more critical that the barcode labels are placed as straight as possible. These issues have only occurred at the DACS barcode reader so far. Ran 30 presets for most of the day. Put in old parameters and presets and had an issue with the barcode scanner pulling up the wrong preset. When writing settings from USB to DACS it didn't over ride the preset barcodes for some reason. Removed the CF card inside the DACS and deleted what was INSIDE the wctemp folder and placed the backed up parameters in the folder put the CF card back in and powered up and had no problems with the wrong preset being pulled from the barcode scanner. Earlier this morning we had some NoRead2 errors occur due to the barcodes not setup for a preset. They weren't on the list. After almost half an hour we had found that the NoRead2 errors would show up when it should have been NoRead1 because it didn't see the label. We did a test by running 4 boxes in a row and leaving a gap behind the 4th box. The second and fourth boxes would be flipped around so that the barcode wouldn't be read by the scanner. First box ok, second, NoRead2 (should be NoRead1), third ok, fourth NoRead1. The gap on the last box proved that the cycle time for a case is very tight. When the scanner can't read the barcode it exceeds the cycle time which overlaps into the next cycle. We also did a test with a good barcode, bad barcode, gap, good case and it read NoRead1 like it should.

Tried moving around the barcode scanner along with the emitter/transmitter photo eyes to see if we could prevent overlapping but had no success in doing so. Tried speeding up the conveyors on the DACS but the tolerance is so tight that sometimes it would so up as NoRead1 but mostly NoRead2. This issue isn't stopping the line from working at all but the error message is misleading. Had a conference call with Jim, Walt and, Daiko to discuss what we can do from here about fixing the error code. Daiko will forward on the information to IJ. Travelled to airport.
