Friday 4/4 - Adjusted the Detect Delay Time from 884msec to 874msec and expanded the margin to 120msec on the single preset on Lane 2A. We are working with IJ on a solution for Reject Confirm, Conveyor restart after error, and Dynamic Calibration. Only settings that should be adjusted are the margin and delay time sparingly. I would recommend using the automatic settings tab in the settings for the preset for Detect Timing Auto Adjust and maybe adjusting that time if needs be by +/- 10msec on the Detect Delay timing. The margin auto sets to 58 or 52 depending on the belt speed per preset. I have them around 100-120 without many issues. Please contact us if situation worsens. Travel to another customer.
Wednesday 4/2 - Travel to Duluth, GA from Atlanta, GA. Heavy traffic.

Thursday 4/3 - Conducted trials on several products. Ran soy burgers, breaded and grilled chicken, beef steak, chicken nuggets, chicken patties, meatballs, and soy breakfast patties. Customer is currently working on possibily purchasing 2 IX's. A 65100 and another 4075. Able to pick up 0.5mm SUS Ball on several of the products and at a minimum 1.0mm SUS. Was able to pick up SUS wire on all at a minimum of 0.7mm SUS. Glass at 5.0mm. Customer was impressed. Left site to go to another customer in Atlanta, GA.

Friday 4/4 - Arrived on site with the customer explaining that they're having issues with the e-stop circuit and power supply. Customer installed a power supply that isn't an Ishida approved part. I explained that to the customer that they need to put the proper power supply in even if it matches up with the appropriate V IN and V OUT + A. (which it does) Checked e-stop circuit and found that when the e-stops and doors are open that the voltage drops across the series connections. Checked the K4 timing relay and found no issues with it along with the SSR for the heaters. Voltage coming into the ATLAS is 277 across all 3 phases. Voltages from the TX are 200V on all three phases. Tried replacing SCU1 and then SCU2 without any changes. Double checked the E-stop connections. Found a load of cookie dust caked into the terminal of one side of the NC contact of the estop that was keeping the circuit open on the SCU1 XJ12 pins 5&7 connection that is NC on the drawings. Checked voltage at 5&7 and saw that I was getting +24VDC which it should not as that would mean the circuit is NO when it should be NC. Used contact cleaner on the Estop contacts and the connection was restored. Powered up ATLAS and tested functions. Customer will need to order a new U2 +24VDC Power Supply, a standoff for supporting SCU1 that broke when it was replaced by customer. Saturday 4/5 - Travel.

Wednesday 4/9- Ceia was displaying Probe Fault (5) then would attempt to do an auto balance but would fail and then attempt it again. DM is set to 0. Changed DM to 4 and the faults went away. Changed all products to DM 4 (with the exception of the DEFAULT program which shouldn't be used for production). Tested reworked product of peanuts, caramel, and nugent and was able to pick up 1.0mm FE, 1.5mm NFE, and 1.5mm SS316 and reject them. Filled out Validation Rep.

Friday 4/11- Customer states that mempry has been erased somehow. Did a debug init. In case of a bug causing this. Had several issues with the weights fluctuating. Unseated and reseated the ADC board and now they're more stable. WH5 load cell reads +20g higher than it should. Replaced load cell. Spans and zeroes properly. Spanned all load cells. WDU5 needs cam sensors and a DDU board. There is no air dryer installed and there is heavy water damage due to this. The customer is ordering one to be installed. CCW runs all functions. Having customer order RCU, ADC, Motherboard, and a spare DUC.
Saturday 4/12- Started installation of TSC-RVS. Installed HUB and ethernet connections. Moved the RCU support bracket and frames to appropriate sides for operator access.
Sunday 4/13- Installing MES kits. Replaced conveyor on Line 3 for a more narrow one.
Monday 4/14- Connecting interface cables for all TSC-RVS. Updated software on several bagmakers. Tested interlocks between Douglas GUACP and TSC. Installed shakers on lines 2 and 9.
Tuesday 4/15- Startup for production on all lines. Monitored production of Doritos and Santita's Tortillas. Made adjustments to several flow controls on reject tables.
Wednesday 4/16- Continued running and monitoring production.
Monday 4/21- Picked up rental car for early morning drive tomorrow.

Tuesday 4/22- Travel. 2 CCW-RZ are being requested by the customer to increase the production speeds. Current setup has 35 degree chutes and is using 6L size hoppers. Installed a make shift crash tube which decreased the product caught in seal substantially. Running both CCW-RZ at 70bpm currently. Still have some product caught in seal but much better than it was.

Wednesday 4/23- Customer states that they had to slow down the bagger to 65bpm due to product in seal. Created a "crash curtain" and welded the bancollan on the corners to make it more ridged. Installed it on the CCW and observed production. The curtains are a tad bit high but I don't want it to cause any bridging. The product is hitting the curtain when a larger load is being dumped from the WH and it is keeping the product from crashing into the other side of the transition funnel. Will return tomorrow to see how night shift went.

Thursday 4/24- Made another curtain in a cross shape and installed it on the CCW. Works better than the triangle shaped one. Running bagger at 75bpm with no glaring issues. I would recommend fabricating a permanent cross curtain to keep product from swirling and crashing into each other. Also raising the baggers at least a few inches. The closer the bagger is to the CCW the less the drop time is required resulting in better efficiency and speed. Looked at Line 10 CCW's. Several heads were turned off and I reactivated them and only found that #5 on Scale 1 has a drive arm issue causing the WH to not open fully. Operators maybe turning off heads instead of making proper adjustments to time and amplitude if stepper motor errors are the issue than observing what the problem is.

Friday 4/25- Customer said that the line had its best day after the modifications were made. Ran 75bpm. Removed the crash curtain to jot down the dimensions so a permanent one can be made. Line 10 CCW-NZ Scale 1 head 12 has zero errors, check stop gap. Head 5 set screw for the WH drive arm is possibly loose and why the hopper gate barely opens and flutters. Same for WH 5 on scale 2. Line 18 drive unit 3 needs stop gap checked or possible load cell replacement.
Monday 4/28- Picked up rental car for early morning travel.

Tuesday 4/29- Travel to plant. Customer wants to have a preset made for 5lbs and 1.3kg. They tried to do it but had some issues. I created new presets for 40bpm for both. Customers preset had too tight of a tolerance (25g for chicken drumsticks) Opening the tolerance more will allow the CCW to make combinations. Tested 5lbs of drumsticks which will work fine. Travelled home. *Travel time may increase due to severe storms in the area.*

To help prevent overscale and overweight errors please have the worker upstairs on the mezzanine stop putting too much product into the hoppers. Certain products get jammed but the worker doesn’t need to shove product into hoppers when that set of hoppers isn't asking for product (vibrating and the shutter drive arm is up) This will increase efficiency greatly! Target weight: 2,267g, Upper Limit: 60g. Weigher speed: 28 is what was ran with no issues.
Thursday 5/1- Spent the whole day tuning RF 6-12. 1-5, 14 tuned when arrived on site. Had issues with vibration once the top of the scale was reinstalled.
Friday 5/2- Retuned several feeders as close to natural frequency as possible.
Saturday 5/3- Finished tuning RF. Tested all RF with the top of the scale installed. All RF vibrate very well when good RF pan is installed. Some of the pans are in
bad shape resulting in poor vibration and amplitude. Customer wasn't on site for the weekend. Left to return home for a personal matter.

Tuesday 5/6- Calibrated DACS-W and WN (6) checkweighers. All DACS are in good condition and weigh accordingly. Assisted with maintenance worker startup of CCW-M (4). Adjusted stop gap on 9 and 15. WDU#1 on scale 3 needs a new cam roller (part number 060-5312-05) it is causing stepper motor issues.                                                                                      Traveled to another customer in the area.
Monday 5/5- Dropped off rental car and headed to another customer.

Wednesday 5/7- RF's 3,4,6,10,11 were not vibrating product well at all. Went through and re tuned 3,4,6,11. 10 wasn't vibrating due to a bad AC Fuse board. Had customer order a new AC Fuse board for next day. Tested with all the RF's attached with frozen block of fish and they all ran the product across the pan.

Thursday 5/8- Replaced AC Fuse board and now all RF's work. Having issues running product on 3,4,6,11. They will more than likely need new coils, shafts for the        pan connection, covers, (upper and lower) and a new block (plate for the coil) as some of them have been damaged. I manipulated the pans by only securing the outmost (towards discharge) clamp and left the back part (DF side) unconnected. This has helped move product across the pan as a temporary solution only. Travel home

Monday 5/12- Travel to customer. Tested DACS-G and Ceia for production startup. Ceia stand alone unit was wired up improperly. Had 208VAC incoming when it needed 120VAC. Inverter blew a capacitor. Had another sent overnight for repairs tomorrow. Conducted training on DACS and Ceia combo units. Tested running 14 oz and 5 lbs bags of peanuts through the metal detector and DACS. Picked up 1.5/1.5/2.0mm FE/NFE/SS with both sizes running the same preset. DACS should get windcovers installed for both units due to air causing some flucuation on the weights. It reads good when running but for better accuracy it is recommended.

Tuesday 5/13- Trained operators on creating a program on the DACS and Ceia and how to auto learn product and make changes to presets on the DACS when it is needed. Replacement inverter was installed and tested functions of Ceia. Proper voltage in @120VAC. Filled out checklists and traveled home.

Wednesday 5/14- Assisted with placing the mezzanine and CCW. Installed Ceia on CCW. Found that the Ceia is too close to the CCW and the bayonet chute is lifting the lower poly discharge chute from its support pins used to hold it.

Thursday 5/15- Fastback has no platform for it to rest on. Customer is getting another contractor to make a platform for it for installation next week. I cut 15mm off the top of the bayonet chute and raised the support pins to hold the lower poly DC so it would fit. Found that the RS is too close to the lower poly DC and cannot fully cycle.

Friday 5/16- Replaced the 4 threaded rods measuring 145mm from threaded end to end with 100mm ones for securing the RS. Since doing that the RS can fully cycle and it is even on all areas of the lower poly DC when it is at a 180 degree stroke and lightly taps it. Powered up Ceia and had to do a TA autolearn so that it wouldn't cause any false alarms. No product to test yet but ran test samples of 1.5/1.8/2.0mm FE/NFE/SS with success. Will return next week for finish installation of the Fastback, Ceia, and CCW.

Tuesday 5/20- Travel to plant. Arrived on site with the CCW working fairly well since talking with the customer yesterday afternoon. Created a new preset for running onion rings 795g. Demostrated to customer how to make changes to time and amps, weight, and other factors for running production. Running at 100% eff @30bpm 795g TW. Ran potato wedges 1020g @30bpm 100% eff. Assisted with customer copying presets to other preset numbers and using it as a benchmark to make fine adjustments to each product type and weight. Production ran perfectly with 100% eff throughout the day.

Thursday 5/22/14- Platform for Fastback has arrived and has been anchored. Assisted with placing Fastback on platform and secured it to it. PSD was signed. Waiting for 480VAC 3 phase, 208VAC and 120VAC subpanel to be installed for supply voltages for Fastback, CCW, and Ceia. They will also need 10-36VDC input voltage for the photo eye which controls upstream bucket conveyor to stop when Fastback pan is full.

Friday 5/23/14- Electricians are still working on building a sub panel for incoming voltage to equipment. CCW and Ceia have been tested by using a dropcord last week. 480VAC has been supplied to Fastback. Checked motor rotation. Once bucket conveyor has been fully put together the Fastback will need to be leveled properly along with installing the communication wires for the photo eye and the run signal to the CCW. Customer has been notified to contact service office if any further support is needed.
Saturday 5/24- Travel to customer. Arranged all parts to be installed in the morning due to sanitation in the production area.

Sunday 5/25- Installed new SF Troughs, Screws, DF pans, PH, and deflector pads on both 70 size screw feeders. Ran whole chicken breast through it smoothly. Replaced SF Troughs, deflector pans, and screws on both 30 size screw feeders. Ran whole chicken breast throught it althought it usually runs tenders, it did run pretty well with the larger product. Speed was at 30bpm for all screw feeder scales.

Tuesday 5/27- Travel to plant. ITPS was already installed and powered up upon arrival. Did a checkout before beginning production of 283g of potato chips. Running very well with no issues. Customer had an ATLAS-200R that they were wanting to be rebuild. Worked on assessing the parts needed to put it back on the production floor.
Wednesday 5/28- Continued auditing ATLAS and compiled a list of replacement parts. Monitored production of new ATLAS-233R no issues.
Thursday 5/29- Putting together parts list and knocking off unnecessary items. Completed install checklists for CCW-R and ATLAS-233R. Will return when parts have been shipped. Traveled home.

entries.city: Picked up rental car and traveled to Lynchburg
body: Saturday 5/31- Installed ATLAS-203R. Updated software for the CCW-M RCU: S2574. and WCU: S2575 to work with Douglas RCC. ATLAS has updated software installed already, DMU: M5126H, MCU1: M1592B, MCU2: M1490J, SCU1: M1596A, SCU2: M1582F, RCU: W1095C.
Sunday 6/1- Filled out ATLAS checklist. Check interface between all equipment. TSC and ATLAS had IP conflict errors so the address for the RCU's have been changed on the TSC RCU to 192.168.0.2.

Monday 6/2- Ran production of 28.3g Doritos @ 130bpm. Customer is working with Don Carver and the Lititz office with getting a nitrogen toggle switch installed on the ATLAS. Customer is having an issue with the TSC restarting after the case packer stops. At times it doesn't auto restart. It is possible that the issue is that the case packer (Blueprint) may not being sending a healthy signal output when it has an error and is cleared. When an error such as a case jam or low boxes occurs the TSC restarts just fine. Customer will look into it and may request assistance from us at a later time. Updated settings on the CCW-M and ATLAS-203R onto a CF card. Finished Install checklist for ATLAS. Found during production that the lower stainless discharge chute that connects onto the legs 3 & 5 has a flat edge that product is hitting when WH 3 and 4 opens at times. It increases the amount of time it takes to drop to the RCC which can result in under & overweights Travel home to another assignment.

Tuesday 6/3- Arrived at customer with production running for the CCW-RV and all 3 Ceia MD. Customer is having issues picking up 0.9/1.4/1.4mm FE/NFE/SS test samples. Able to pick up 1.0/1.5/1.5 without issue. Line 5 MD has 480V and 120V running through the same conduit near the MD head. Customer will address.

Wednesday 6/4- Conducted training with operators on CCW-RV. Line was down due to boiler issue. Was able to test product through the Ceia and pick up the samples of 0.9/1.4/1.4 using DM 2 and SE 297 for both Line 4 and 5. Conduit has been fixed so only 120 VAC is going through it so the noise has dropped a lot.

Thursday 6/5- Tested Line 4 & 5 Ceia's and both passed validation by picking up 30 tests each 0.9FE, 1.4NFE, 1.4SS with product. Trained 1st and 2nd shift operators on CCW-RV production. When the line starts up particularly the vacuum for the scrap rework next to line 5 the Ceia will alarm momentarily but since the vacuum stays on and must stay on during production the signal flat lines after a few seconds and works perfectly afterwards. Monitored production of Lines 4 & 5 and saw no issues with properly made product running. Large clumps will cause the Ceia to alarm which is beneficial as this product needs to be removed from the line anyways. Large clumps being product that is improperly molded and massed together with other improperly molded tortellini.
Monday 6/9- Travel to customer. Installed the first IX-GA (100040633) and completed the survey checklist. Tested reject and set timing. Installed second IX-GA
(90431) completed survey checklist and tested reject and set timing.
Tuesday 6/10- Conducted training on operation level and new product setup. Ran 18oz of chicken nuggets. Conveyor speed at 45m/min. Friesens conveyor had an
issue with the cylinder for the retracting belt not moving fast enough. Removed flow controls and put the line straight into the fitting. Works much faster. With the
current product of chicken nuggets, it runs best at 45m/min for the IX belt and 40.6Hz on the reject conveyor with the reject settings of 2000mm length and 650ms
on time. The product is fed to the IX from a 45 degree incline belt that doesn't space or flatten bags for smoother transistion or better inspection results with fewer
false detections, onto a 45 degree declined stainless chute onto the belt. Product isn't at all uniform when entering the IX. If the product was spaced properly or at
least straight going into the IX inspection results would produce fewer false detections.
Wednesday 6/11- Conducted training for QA, production, and maintenance. Toned down the sensitivities since metal is the priority. Able to pick up 0.6mm SS re-
gularly. Made backups of settings and saved them to the CF cards inside each IX. Monitored production of chicken strips and chicken patties. Able to pick up test
Thursday 6/12- Stopped by to check on production before returning home. Travel home.

Friday 6/13- Travel to customer. Assisted with swapping of CCW-M and a CCW-NZ from lines 5 and 12. Had to change DIPSW on both ATA so that it would properly fault the right CCW when it is in that mode. FMD on Line 5 is having issues. However the signal is received when metal is detected but the MD won’t hold to reset.

Monday 6/16- Travel to customer. Upon arrival checked interface wiring and worked on installation checklist. Robert's rep will be on site tomorrow to continue the installation. CCW-RS was brought from another factory and we assisted them with the install as well.

Tuesday 6/17- Went over production screens with maintenance (operator and site engineer) and continued on installation checklist. Tested interlock signals with the Robert's. Robert's is having air supply issues. Will return in the morning to continue install and production.

Wednesday 6/18- Robert's is still being worked on. During this time I conducted training for 3 operators on operator screens and production. Assisted with startup of the CCW-RS running 400g of pet food at 45wpm (Stroke on Demand, 35 on bagger) Vibratory conveyor won't operate due to excessive product load on top of it. Plant will replace the conveyor with an auger screw type conveyor in the next few days to a week. Ordered a touch screen replacement for the CCW-RS as the top of the screen is non-responsive.

Thursday 6/19- Trained 2 more operators on running production. Touch screen replaced. Customer will call for service if necessary next week when new conveyor is installed. Made presets for 100g,171g, 567g, 3000g. Travel home.

entries.customer: Heat and Control (Fresh Express IE DS Training)
body: Monday 6/23- Travel to office. Installed new tamps and jockey wheel on DS. Tested HMI and functions before Fresh Express arrives next day.
Tuesday 6/24- Conducted training on IE DS with operators and maintenance. Went over operations.
Wednesday 6/25- Conducted training with maintenance on maintenance screens and functions.

Thursday 6/26- Conducted training on electrical systems and schematics troubleshooting. Had an issue with the M320 motion controller not working. QA16 breaker was tripped causing that issue. Once it was reengaged it worked fine.
Friday 6/27- Assessed machine, took further notes. Travel home.

Monday 6/30- Travel to customer. Arrived on site and began rounding parts to install on (2) CCW-R and (2) 260E. Picked up David Ward from the airport. Returned to plant to set the agenda for tomorrow.

Tuesday 7/1- Worked with contractors to set up power to equipment. 480VAC 3p to both 260-E 480VAC 1p to both CCW. Photo eye on each 260-E will not be in use as they have a level sensor staged above the back of the 260-E and will be choke feeding it. Conduit is being ran to accommodate for power and interface wiring. Worked on installation checklists.

Wednesday 7/2- Conduit is still being ran to all equipment. Temporary power has been placed on Fastback. Worked with contractors to install AB PowerFlex 525 to test operation of Fastback. Was able to test rotation of FB and simulate calling for product by jumping 2&11. Informed customer that we would need to have air piped for the TH's on both scales.

Thursday 7/3- Tested the other FB and checked rotation. Received TechPub for inverter parameters and entered those in. Advised customer of what is needed to be ready for the next phase of operations. Conduit is still being ran. Instructed contractors to run main and control power in separate conduits for the Fastbacks. Fastback needs 3P 480VAC + PE and 2 wire shielded cable for controls. CCW needs air piped to TH. The regulators are no where to be found along with the span weights. Control wires to CCW can wait to be ran until we return and conduit is ready to the bagger. Control wiring can be ran as soon as the conduit is ready for the Fastback. Contractor can terminate control wires for CCW and FB by terminating them on 2&11 on FB terminal block and 30&31 on CCW Relay board. Informed contact to call and schedule for return to interface equipment once conduit has been installed and wiring ran. Customer found regulators that should work for the TH. Having a quote made for span weights, timing jig for FB, and blue box of install parts. Travel home.
Sunday 7/6- Travel to plant. Installed CCW-R and Ceia MD.
Monday 7/7- Conducted training on CCW with operators.
Tuesday 7/8- Tested interface with Triangle bagger and did span weight production. Tested 510.3g of cereal mix. 66g of cherries, 423g of flakes and granola mix, 20g of almonds @40bpm.
Wednesday 7/9- Continued production of 510.3g of cereal mix. Had error signal on 82&83 terminated to Triangle bagger to put reject product into its own bag.

Thursday 7/10- Continued production of 510.3g of cereal mix. Made adjustments to timings WH-PH, BH-WH, PH-RF. Some of the crumbs are sliding out of the hopper doors and getting in the seal of the bag. Customer may need to get a TH to help keep the charge together. Monitored production. Will return next week for start of production.

Monday 7/14- Production delayed due to inventory issues with product. Ran 40bpm 512g of Honey Oats Almond Cherry blend. Cherries have been causing a lot of issues with sticking to hoppers and to each other.
Tuesday 7/15- Continued running 512g of the same product @40bpm. Monitored production and made changes to timings, times and amps, weight on DF. Product flow is getting better with changes.

Wednesday 7/16- A/C is running inside the CCW enclosure. The air is much cooler and the cherries are not sticking as bad as they have been since startup. A/C isn't having an adverse affect on the product so far. Ran production very well.

Thursday 7/17- Continued production. CCW is running solid with a hiccup every now and then. Almonds run such a small amount of the target weight (20.1g out of 512g) that it can be difficult to keep the flow even with tight tolerances to the target weight (2g upper 1.5g lower on 20.1g TW) overall it runs efficiently @98.6%
Friday 7/18- Validated (2) T/MS21 and (1) T/PLVMS21 metal detectors.
Monday 7/21- Powered up CCW and tested functions and I/O. Completed install checklist.
Tuesday 7/22- Waiting for electricians to get power and interfaces hooked up to finish installation.
Wednesday 7/23- Supervised wiring of interfaces. Awaiting power up of ATLAS and CCW's for tomorrow.
Thursday 7/24- Updated chips for APEX bagger for MES kits. Continued with installation of ATLAS and CCW's. Travel home.

entries.customer: Heat and Control (TH Foods and Frito-Lay)
body: Monday 8/4- Travel to Hayward. Began preparations for TH Foods demo.
Tuesday 8/5- Tested functions of the ATLAS-202. Waiting for Videojet to arrive to install the printer.
Wednesday 8/6- Installed Videojet and ran 8.375" wide bags at 75bpm. Tested seal integrity. Pressure set to 1200lbs temps at 320 for the back and 300 for the end seals.

Thursday 8/7- Prior to customer arrival had issues with Videojet ribbon breaking. Seals on the bag weren't holding well and had to change the pressure to 1400 to guarantee that there will be no leaks. Ran FAT successfully.
Friday 8/8- Packed up ATLAS to ship it when customer requests it.
Saturday 8/9- No work. Returning to office Monday 8/11.
Tuesday 8/12- Tested 1oz of cheetos @ 150bpm. Checked weights for accuracy and they're +/- 0.5g. Removed bagger and placed RCC bagger under CCW.

Wednesday 8/13- Had to remove RCU from the bagger and place on the CCW support frame for full motion of RCU to be used. Customer will checkout stackup of the ITPS with RCC machine and work with Randy Blair for any modifications it may need at a later time.

Monday 8/18- Travel to customer. Began updating RCU software to W-0282A. Also updated MCU to N-2753A. Had an RCU-MEM error. IP addresses needed to be set to default. Installed DRV N-2754 ADC N-2247B REJ N-2755. Updated wiring to PLC and DRV board. Was unable to operate DACS. Couldn't keep the belts on. Kept getting overload errors on all conveyors. Tried to revert back to older software but it would show up as program load error on the RCU screen when trying viaUSB.

Tuesday 8/19- Continued with reverting software to original. Kept getting power error upon power up when RCU was loaded. Replaced DRV board and was able to get past the error. Had to turn on DIPSW 2-1 on DRV and ADC board for program to load via USB (DRV/ADC/REJ programs). Still having the same errors. Made text and prm file backups and emailed them to office for testing purposes.

Wednesday 8/20- Tried disabling additional conveyor and removing all connections to it. (PLC and run signal) Still have the same errors. Reinstalled original DRV and installed latest settings for DRV/ADC/REJ and the conveyors now move properly. Replaced REJ board on rejector with the DRV sent from Lititz office. Updated software for the REJ. New software has a bug which is causing the transportation error not to appear on the RCU and stops the conveyor when the photo sees a pack that didn't reject. Production is running smoothly otherwise. Tom Zwaan will be here tomorrow morning.

Thursday 8/21- Began installation of IE DS. Was able to get the C&P along with the DS itself mostly put together. Terminated clutch sensor wiring along with E-Stop power. Will continue installation tomorrow with leveling and squaring up equipment.

Friday 8/22- Leveled and squared up equipment. The Ethernet cable that connects to the HMI will have to be replaced as the length is not long enough. An extra 8' will be enough. Travel home to return Sunday evening.
Monday 8/25- Drilled holes in the HMI to fit it on the post. Connected the denester end of the C&P to the carriage end of conveyor.

Tuesday 8/26- Put dielectric grease inside all sensors and heat shrinked them to keep water from getting in. Ran ethernet cable for HMI for tray filler. Modified frame for denester side conveyor and removed the cross bar on the end closest to the carriage side.
Wednesday 8/27- Replaced RCU harness for the CCW as the original was too short. Ran and fit TH harnesses to size also. Installed HMI.
Thursday 8/28- Wired interface wires from CCW to DS. Powered on DS and had a comm issue. Ethernet cable will need to be replaced as we ran a patch cable to the HMI from the control panel.
Friday 8/29- Ran new patch cable through wireways. Adjustments made to Lane B tamp and carriage.

Saturday 8/30- Made adjustments to Lane A tamp and carriage. Connected peg and chain and set the timing. Having issues with motion controller M320 error is popping up. Will have to get logged onto the PLC to figure out the issue.
Sunday 8/31- No work. 8 hour minimum charge.
Monday 9/1- Installed change parts for 5oz and tested operation. Having issues with the motion controller M320 error.
Tuesday 9/2- Was able to update the PLC program on the DS. This also took care of the M320 motion controller error. Installed brackets for the denester.
Wednesday 9/3- Tested 16oz carriage. Installed denesters and tested functions.
Thursday 9/4- Installed the rest of the guards. Ran product through scale and DS in drain mode. Travel home.
Friday 9/5- Travel to plant. Filled out and completed Ceia validations for both Ceia metal detectors. Travel home.
Tuesday 9/16- Travel to plant. Installed new pans and removed old counterweights and replaced with new for 3680 and added new counterweights to 3689.
Wednesday 9/17- Electricians are wiring up the drives and solenoids for slide gates for testing. Bumped motors for the fastbacks that were adjusted. Travel to another assignment.
Wednesday 9/17- Travel to customer to be on site before noon tomorrow.

Thursday 9/18-  Arrived on site and completed Ceia validations of both T/MS21 metal detectors. They both detect metal and the belt stops when sample sizes of 3.0mm FE, 3.5mm NFE, and 5.0mm SS316 is used. Travel home.

Saturday 9/20- Travel to customer. Attempted to install mods to the APEX but the block that the ACME threaded rod goes through doesn't fit properly for manual control of the back seal in/out movement. Software for the CCW-M was up to date already but I reinstalled it for good measure. Updated the RCU software on the APEX from M0518C to M0525A as the APEX has a MES kit installed. Unable to see what software is installed on the MCU and SCU boards due to the boards being made for an ATLAS as the APEX boards can't be used for RCC. There is only one way to update the boards and I do not have the means to do it. RCC has been running prior to visit. According to Walt, the software was up to date prior to my visit. Currently awaiting word on getting the proper parts to complete the mods. Installed the original equipment and tested to make sure they could run production. Will need to return once resolved. Travel home.
Wednesday 9/24- Travel to customer. Weather increased travel time.

Thursday 9/25- Started up 419g of Mini Rolos running @65WPM. DACS-003 weigh range is capped at 300g. If they want to inspect the weight of the bag on this line they will need to replace the load cell from a 003 to a 012 and initialize the DACS to a 012. They’re only running 4 shifts of this product so they will make do with what they have. Bridging issues as the product charge coming down is large and the aperture is very small for it to fit into the bag. Increased the stagger to 70ms which has helped. Saturday 10/25- Travel to customer site. Replaced the block and threaded rod to fit in a new manual back seal adjustment assembly. Fit the smallest and largest formers to make sure that it will work. When the dial is reading 000.0 it is at the point that the backseal is touching the smallest former. When a larger former is installed the number will be larger for the starting point. The adjustment will always be a larger number than 000.0. A good starting point for running 5.5" bag width is 006.1 and as the bag sizes become wider the number on the dial is directly proportional to that. There is a collar on the shaft for the back seal that was supposed to be used to "lock in" an adjusment to keep it within the neccesary limit (i.e., 000.0 - 030.0) but it can't go any lower than 071.2 due to the collar being at the end of the shaft diameter that it fits on to. The collar has a 12mm diameter and the diameter before it turns to the thread portion of the shaft is 16mm. If needed a collar with a 16mm diameter could be fit to keep it within the desired limits for the backseal.

Sunday 10/26- Customer was explaining issues with the APEX since it was updated to run RCC. The boards have been changed from APEX to ATLAS style boards. This can cause a problem for when they need to replace a defective board they can no longer put the proper software onto it without using special equipment to do so. They have asked that we make it so they could install software onto boards as the ATLAS machines do with the use of the programming board (DMU to MCU/SCU). Also they no longer have use of the switch on the former feed roller that tells the film spindle to retract when they switch from big to small size bags. This is due to a several things. On SCU2 XJ6 pins 1-4 have no voltage on them. On the drawing it shows that one side from the SCU1 XJ7 is NC and the other NO. The NC side should have +24VDC on the solenoid to keep the spindle retracted if set for large film. When the micro switch is engaged on the former feed roller it should then close the NO side and push out the spindle to use small bags. Temporally they've installed a toggle switch to retract or engage the solenoid spindle. Also they've had to keep the former film roller set for use on large bags (By having the roller flipped closer to the former) so they can run small bags on the APEX because if they try to use the former roller positioning motor it bottoms out because the special formers they use for RCC have a much smaller slope (higher degree of incline) from the bottom back side of the former to the top where the film is then pulled down and formed into a bag before being sealed on the back seal. This wasn't an issue until the APEX boards were replaced with ATLAS style boards. If changes to software are needed IJ needs to keep in mind that if they still want to use the switch for the former feed roller that they will have to make mechanical changes so that the it won't bottomout and cause a servo overload error requiring the power to be cycled. Customer is able to make different width bags by keeping the former feed roller in the forward position and then using the toggle switch to move between small and large films. Travel home.

Thursday 5/21- At customer site. Customer was having issues with weight fluctuations on the DACS-G-S015-34. I saw the weight jump between -6g to +6g with the belt stop I did a memory initialize and the weight became much more stable (-0.5g to +0.4g) While the belt was running and flagging the photo eye the weight would be between -1.85 and +1.85g. This checkweigher is 300mm wide for the weigh table. Ran several packages of 474g bag of beef jerky. The machine was quoted to run at 85 packs per minute with an accuracy of +/- 2.0 - 4.0 grams which it achieves in the shop. Out on the line there is interference from wind in the area and the needing to create a gap from the 90d interlox belt that feeds onto the DACS. Instead of running 40m/min on all the belts the configuration the customer has is 45m/min on the infeed, 50 on the weigh, and 65 on reject tables. In the shop I was able to run the belts at 40m/min with a theoretical max of 88 packs per minute and achieved a maximum weight of 477.85g a minimum of 476.25g, an average weight of 476.78g, and a standard deviation of 0.378g of an actual weight of 476.9g bag. Some possible solutions, which foremost be to try to lower the speed of the DACS to achieve a much more accurate weight. Another would be to lower the photo eye and decrease the bag length without it causing a double bag error. It is possible that the weighing time calculation is on the edge of time needed to formulate the weight. Reducing this would give it more time to calculate. If metal detector is still experiencing electrical noise issues, the following practices can help alleviate the interference: Make sure that the motor frame is insulated from the metal support. Checked on the ATLAS about issues with the centering of the hole punch and tear notch. Found that the fixture that is used for very small bags was installed backwards. The fixture which is a spacer should be installed first onto the film spindle then the film roll. When running empty bags the film will move side to side due to no weight in the bag to keep it from being moved around easily. This will result in the hole punch not being centered. The tear notch needed to have the punch tip rotated to the top side so it would cut the notch in the bag closer to the top. Thursday 7/28- Customer states that Ceia has difficulty running certain products. There is a lot of noise on the line. Product signal without product is tripping the alarm signal. Main power to the Ceia is 240VAC. It is fed from the Smalley cabinet. There is no ground wire tied to the PE which would bond it to the frame. They will need to run a separate main from source with a ground from earth. Do not daisy chain ground from other equipment. Motor needs to be "floating" also which means to ground motor to ground away from other equipment. If noise is still an issue it would be best practice to use an EMI filter or line reactor on the input side of main power to invertor. The output side of the invertor to the motor can have a ferrite core installed with the wires twisted close together to prevent radiating noise. Also, using shielded cable from the output side of the invertor to the motor would help greatly. Do these things will help tremendously. Made a change to the ADS (Filter adjust) from 0 to -3. This allowed production to be able to run without a lot of noise. Went to lunch and returned and the noise level was barely noticeable. Had to adjust the photo eye which tells the CCW to cycle. Ran into a cycle overlap issue. If the photo eyes (there are two, one for each side of the CCW (C1 and C2)) sync meaning, both of them see a carton at the same time it will confuse the cartoneer and the CCW. More than likely what is happening is that the PLC program has the photo eyes in parallel to a register that determines which side the signal to the CCW goes to. If they both sync at the same time two pulses go to the CCW at the same time causing the issue. When the photo eyes are not in sync there are no issues with cycle overlaps.

Tuesday 1/31- CCW-RV running production with no issues. Checked on transducer parts. Customer believes that they have been installing the wrong size transducer. There is one that has a longer wire (I can't confirm, we assumed) and the one that has a shorter one is believed to have been installed and replaced many times. Confirmed the part that should be used (632656B) they were using (632450B that was replaced by 632450C that also broke) Line went down for changeover and replaced the transducer cable. Saw that the old one somehow got snagged on the cam follower which snapped the wire(**** see picture below). Installed the new one and made sure that it couldn't get snagged on anything. Calibrated the span on the transducer to ensure that it would read the proper reading on Simplot's HMI(**** please read my concerns below) . Observed production and checked that the level sensor would cause the rev gate to adjust for the product depth. Travel to Fargo for early morning flight. Trained an electronic tech on circuit boards and RCU screens. (The transducer that was installed was (632656B)

As myself and an electronic tech were beginning to change the transducer I was unable to see how he had it installed as he removed it but did see that it was installed incorrectly. I've attached a picture and to see how it was installed, flip the transducer 180 degrees vertically. (The picture is showing that it's correctly installed but invert it so see how it was installed by the tech) This picture is from a known good RevGate so I used this as a reference.

I found this to be an odd position for the wire to be caught into. That wire is tension loaded and should always be forced against the drum frame itself. It's possible that due to being installed incorrectly that it could have created enough slack that it was caught on the cam follower? Speculation, but if anything is installed wrong, it's possible?

Simplot has their own controls group who do not use what I'm familiar with seeing, program wise that PSI uses. When attempting to check the 4-20mA reading I found that my fuse was blown on my multimeter. Raul from Simplot engineering said that he could see the readout on his HMI and asked me to adjust the span on one of the RevGates and for the new transducer. We were also pressed for time as the line was down longer than they anticipated with other issues and were waiting on me to get this going. The process that he was using to adjust the gates was to set it to 90 degrees and look at the read out on the HMI and then tell it that it is actually at 90. (Don't know the actual formula used) Basically taking the reference point and say that value (or readout from the transducer) is equal to 90 degrees. Then fully open the gate and we adjusted the span until it read zero (which would be close to 20mA or 18.8mA according to the TechPub) I also checked to make sure that the mechanical stops actually stopped it from over extending the transducer wire. Once this was all completed we tested to make sure the level sensor was causing the RevGate to open or close based on the product depth. Production started shortly after and went without issue. Byron from Simplot corporate asked me before I left earlier yesterday that I make sure the gates are calibrated to work with Simplot's controls program, to train one of the electronic techs on the CCW as time permits, and production starts and operates properly.

My concerns are with the program that Simplot uses, If they make adjustments outside of the normal operating range it could cause issues with the equipment. Maybe if this happens again we get with Raul to get a print out of the settings he uses and confirm that it is within the proper operating range that we use.

Thursday 6/29- Customer was reporting that when they run test samples that it would count each sample ran as 2 instead of 1. Saved event buffer for analysis for Ceia to look at. Looking on the o-scope the signal picked up from the sample spikes up high and drops down low and back up high again which leads me to believe that since it dropped below the alarm threshold and above it again that it counted it as 2 hits instead of 1. Speeds are set to maximum. Changed ADS from 0 to -3 and raised SE to 299 and was able to get it to count as 1 per sample dropped. This also cleaned up the noise that was being created from the pulverizer that was across from the unit. Was not able to get it to count 2 per sample dropped since making these changes. (21400204106)

After walking away the adjustments were changed to the old settings. The only adjustments that need to be changed from time to time (based on product size whether baby or large spinach or wet and dry) is the Time and Amps on the RF. There is a guard in place to help prevent product from being shoved to the back of the radial screw feeder and product tends to stick to this also. The guard is a solid circular stainless steel ring and is not embossed (not C4) not sure if that will help if it is changed to C4. Both the double helix and solid body screws were tested and the difference is negligible. The gap between the RF pan and screw is around 10mm. The product itself is around 5mm. Product won’t move across the RF pan if the screw can’t touch it. Modifications to the screws would more than likely be necessary, maybe increasing the screw size diameter by 5mm. Tested 2.2oz of sticky jerky dumping into the PPI Leepack but was unable to get it to run full production due to interface issues. Currently running in Slave mode on the CCW. Tried changing to Stroke but no change. PPI tech will be in tomorrow morning and will get that sorted out first thing. Other issues are with discharging the product. Product has a lot of bounce but also sticky. The discharge chutes are very long (understandably) and the outlet of the discharge chute is hexagonal while the inlet of the transition chute is circular. The diameter of the inlet chute is smaller than the area of the hexagonal outlet so product will hit and stick onto the surface which happens to also not be C4 material. Modifications would have to be made for that item. (unsure if it falls under Leepack or H&C responsibility)
1)DT Pan: 50 degrees may be too aggressive, possibly 40 – 45 degrees.
2)RF screws: The diameter of the screws should be increased 5-7mm larger. (Toby to check with IJ tonight if mods are possible)
3)Transition parts to line up better: A polygonal outler into a round inlet spells trouble.
4)Working with PSG: Will have to solve interface issues when tech arrives tomorrow.

Tuesday 6/4- This morning we found the solid body ring gate that sits above the divider blocks for each individual screw feeder position. It is supposed to help prevent product build up at the entrance to the screw feeder from the DT pan. Installed it and it made little difference. We used some thin stainless steel and made a guard out of it to prevent a mass of product from collecting on top of the screw feeder entrance for position 18. This helped keep product from building up there. The guard is basically a flat piece of stainless, bent to allow some product to get through while keeping the rest of the product on the DT until the screw feeder operates and space is available at the entrance. It is secured by a C-clamp for testing purposes. We made 4 more for a total of 5 and put them on positions 16-20. We have issues with overscales because we only have a 3g window. Compensation is set to 2g because of product sticking on hoppers, chutes, and the transition to the flange below before it goes into the bag. The amount of product that was going through 16-20 was more consistent and even than the rest. We recorded overscales on 16-20 but again with the small window of 3g the product was probably 1-10g over during that error. A total of 45 overscales and 3 were from 16-20. I think we ran around 150 bags. Product sticks a lot to each other and some of the product was larger than 4” which weighs close to target weight. The DT pan spins constantly during production, even when waiting for product. The product that doesn’t make it into the screw feeders can get rolled into a ball during this time. Not sure if we can turn that off during low product. Toby will look into that. Toby asked IJ about the screws being modified. Either they could make them larger or make the screw feeder guides (the pan product rests on before PH) smaller in size to close the gap. Might also see about some bancollon being added to it like a coating or a layer to add thickness to the pan to close the gap. These are some ideas and not confirmations nor would it be readily available. The solid body ring gate has a ring around the body that rests on top of the dividers (blocks that keep product contained inside the screw feeder area). That ring is where someone can drill through to put a bolt and nut to attach the guard where we have a clamp installed currently. I’d rather not drill on the round portion of the ring gate as it’s rounded and would be difficult to do. Also it’s where product would get caught and dragged on. Tomorrow morning, we will run some of the same product but then move onto dry larger product.

Maybe have software programed to see that the infeed signal is inactive for X amount of time to stop. It would probably help with weighing issues if hoppers are cleaned during a break as everything just sticks so easily. Noticed the room temperature increased over time during the day. It was 58 degrees in the morning and warmed up to 70+ degrees at the end of the day. Humidity may also have risen. Sticky product and humidity make things stickier so that doesn't help. Empty judgment weight from 1g to 4g (helps prevent slight under weights and dumping 1-2g crumbs) Error stop pulse count for DTH is 100 BH 125 WH 10 and PH 50. Ran pretty well with a few DTH stepper motor errors. Mostly likely the cause is overscales being rejected that get caught on the tail end of the hopper door closing. When clearing the error the operator should make sure that there is no obstruction if the error occurs again. Multiple errors get logged for the same issue until the obstruction has cleared. Ran 93g of Original beef jerky with occassional zero errors earlier on and less as the day went on after setting changes.

Because 1-4 are on both Y101 and Y102 solenoids are active. If Y101 or Y102 are disconnected (just one of them) N2 flows and shows on the flow meter. Wednesday 12/22- Came on site with CCW set to 90wpm and PPI was @40bpm. Changed both speeds to equal 70 on each machine. Running in slave mode and have not run into any DTH, TH stepper motor errors or cycle overlap errors. Found that when the PPI has not received a dump complete from the CCW it will pulse on and off an interlock signal to allow the CCW to cycle again in hopes of a dump confirm with product to continue motion to the next step on the PPI. That pulse output and speed is static and never changing. If CCW was running at a time faster than the output from the PPI it would cause a cycle overlap or a quicker interlock than what it is used to seeing causing stepper motor errors. Customer is requesting any kind of software that tells the PPI what WPM it is set to so that its internal clock can output interlock signals at the speed the CCW is set to automatically instead of a fixed speed like it is set up as now.

Wednesday 1/5- Ran @75wpm very well until a missed cycle occurred which resulted in a cycle overlap error on the DTH. Interlock signal that is being sent from LeePack isn't timed in sync with CCW speed so when LeePack doesn't recieve a discharge signal it will continue to pulse on and off an interlock signal that may not be synced properly while CCW is attempting to cycle a good dump. Changed CCW speed to 70WPM since in Slave mode it only matters when attempting to find a good dump after a missed cycle or resuming production after low product. Having it at 70WPM hasn't resulted in any cycle overlap errors. At times the LeePack has issues and stops mid cycle (due to critical issues such as high mark / date code / or door opened while running. This causes the interlock to send while not at full production speed and causes the TH and DTH to open out of sequence and causes the TH doors to open hitting the dipping funnel below and causing a TH error and usually causes the TH to become removed from the assembly. When production is running and the LeePack is running well the CCW can reach 75WPM and output high 60's low 70's BPM. Customer released me.
